section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum age to apply for a learner's permit in Colorado?
options: a:14,b:15,c:15 and a half,d:16
note: Colorado allows teens to apply for a learner's permit at age 15. After holding the permit and completing supervised driving requirements, they can apply for a restricted license at age 16.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for drivers age 21 and older in Colorado?
note: Colorado's per se DUI limit is 0.08% BAC for adult drivers. Colorado also has a DWAI (Driving While Ability Impaired) charge at 0.05%–0.079% BAC, which carries lesser penalties but is still a criminal offense.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a steep Colorado mountain grade and have 5 or more vehicles backed up behind you. What are you required to do?
options: a:Speed up to match the flow of traffic,b:Pull into the next available turnout to let traffic pass,c:Activate your hazard lights and continue at your current speed,d:There is no such requirement — you may proceed at any speed
note: Colorado law requires slow-moving vehicles to use turnouts when 5 or more vehicles have accumulated behind them on a two-lane mountain road. Turnouts are provided specifically for this purpose to reduce dangerous passing attempts on steep grades.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving down a steep Colorado mountain grade, what is the recommended technique?
options: a:Ride the brakes continuously to maintain a safe speed,b:Use a lower gear to let engine braking do most of the work, with light brake applications as needed,c:Shift to neutral to conserve fuel and brake as needed,d:Increase speed to reduce the time spent on the steep section
note: On steep downhill grades in Colorado, shift to a lower gear and use engine braking to control your speed. Continuous brake use (riding the brakes) overheats the brakes and can cause brake fade — a sudden loss of braking ability that is extremely dangerous on mountain roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a runaway truck ramp on a Colorado mountain highway indicate?
options: a:A lane for trucks to bypass toll booths,b:An emergency escape route for vehicles with brake failure on steep downgrades,c:A service road for highway maintenance vehicles,d:A designated truck weigh station
note: Runaway truck ramps — filled with deep gravel or sand — are emergency escape routes for vehicles whose brakes have failed on steep mountain downgrades. Passenger vehicles should never use them except in a true brake-failure emergency.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Colorado's GDL program, how many hours of supervised driving must a permit holder complete before applying for a restricted license?
options: a:20 hours including 5 at night,b:30 hours including 5 at night,c:50 hours including 10 at night,d:60 hours including 10 at night
note: Colorado requires 50 hours of supervised driving practice, including at least 10 hours at night, before a permit holder can apply for a restricted (minor) license. This supervised practice builds critical skills before independent driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are approaching a Colorado mountain pass and chains or traction tires are required. What does this mean?
options: a:Traction devices are recommended but optional,b:All vehicles must have either chains or traction tires (4WD, AWD, or winter-rated tires) to proceed,c:Only trucks over a certain weight must comply,d:Chains are required only for vehicles with rear-wheel drive
note: When Colorado posts a traction law requirement at mountain passes, all vehicles must have adequate traction: either chains or tires rated as traction tires (all-season tires with the mountain/snowflake rating, AWD, or 4WD). Ignoring traction requirements can result in a fine and is dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit in Colorado urban areas when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:25 mph,b:30 mph,c:35 mph,d:40 mph
note: Colorado's default urban speed limit is 30 mph where no other limit is posted. Residential neighborhood streets may have lower posted limits — always check for signs. The 30 mph default is a commonly tested fact.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Colorado, what is the BAC level that triggers an additional DWAI (Driving While Ability Impaired) charge — lower than the standard DUI threshold?
note: Colorado uniquely has a DWAI charge that applies when a driver's BAC is between 0.05% and 0.079% — a level where ability may be impaired even though it is below the 0.08% DUI threshold. This is a Colorado-specific law not found in all states.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane Colorado highway, a solid yellow line is on your side of the center. What does this mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted when the road is clear,b:Passing is prohibited — do not cross the line to pass,c:The road ahead has a steep grade,d:Passing is allowed only for vehicles in front of you that are going 10 mph below the limit
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the center line is an absolute prohibition on passing by crossing it. A dashed yellow line on your side indicates passing is permitted when safe. These markings apply throughout Colorado and the nation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a Colorado mountain road during a snowstorm and your windshield begins to fog up. What is the most effective way to clear it?
options: a:Turn on the rear defroster only,b:Use the air conditioner with the temperature set to warm air,c:Open windows briefly to equalize humidity and use the defroster,d:Turn on maximum heater heat directed at the windshield
note: Running the air conditioner with warm air directed at the windshield is the most effective way to clear fogging. The A/C dehumidifies the air, removing moisture that causes fogging. This technique works year-round and is especially important in Colorado's variable mountain weather.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is Colorado's Move Over law requirement when passing a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights?
options: a:Slow to 10 mph and proceed with caution,b:Move one lane away if safe; if not, slow to a safe speed,c:Stop completely until the emergency vehicle leaves,d:Move over only if a law enforcement officer is present
note: Colorado's Move Over law requires drivers to vacate the lane adjacent to any stopped emergency, law enforcement, or highway maintenance vehicle with flashing lights. If a lane change is unsafe, slow to a speed safe for conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum following distance recommended in Colorado for normal driving conditions?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Colorado recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. On mountain roads, in snow, or in heavy traffic, increase following distance to 6 or more seconds — stopping distances on steep grades and slippery surfaces are much longer than normal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian is crossing at a crosswalk in Colorado. You must:
options: a:Slow to 15 mph and proceed if the crosswalk is partially clear,b:Stop and remain stopped until the pedestrian has fully crossed the roadway,c:Yield only if the pedestrian is in your direct lane,d:Honk to alert the pedestrian and proceed
note: Colorado law requires drivers to stop and yield the entire roadway to pedestrians in a crosswalk. You may not proceed until the pedestrian has fully crossed — including any remaining lanes. Pedestrian right-of-way is absolute in a crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally use the shoulder of a Colorado highway to pass a slower vehicle?
options: a:When the vehicle is traveling 10 mph below the speed limit,b:When traffic is backed up and the shoulder is wide enough,c:It is never legal to pass on the shoulder,d:When directed by a law enforcement officer
note: Passing on the shoulder is illegal in Colorado and in most states. The shoulder is reserved for emergency stops and breakdowns only — not for bypassing slow traffic. Using the shoulder to pass is a traffic violation and extremely dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can you turn right on a red light in Colorado?
options: a:No, right turns on red are prohibited statewide,b:Yes, after a complete stop and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it,c:Yes, without stopping if no vehicles are visible,d:Only on designated roads
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Colorado after a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic. Always check for 'No Turn on Red' signs before proceeding. Never turn without first making a complete stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit on Colorado interstate highways in most rural areas?
options: a:65 mph,b:70 mph,c:75 mph,d:80 mph
note: Most Colorado rural interstates have a speed limit of 75 mph for passenger vehicles. Some mountain and urban sections are posted lower. Always obey posted limits — speed limits drop significantly in mountain passes and urban areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Colorado's implied consent law, refusing a chemical test after a DUI stop results in:
options: a:No penalty — refusal is a legal right,b:Immediate license revocation for 1 year on first refusal,c:Only a small fine,d:A warning on your first offense
note: Colorado's implied consent law means that driving on public roads constitutes consent to chemical testing. A first-offense refusal results in a 1-year license revocation that is separate from any DUI charge. Refusal can also be used as evidence of guilt.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a yellow diamond-shaped warning sign mean on a Colorado road?
options: a:A rule you must follow — like a speed limit,b:A potential hazard or road condition ahead requiring extra caution,c:A guide to distances and destinations,d:A construction zone with mandatory reduced speed
note: Yellow diamond-shaped signs are warning signs that alert drivers to potential hazards such as sharp curves, steep grades, and wildlife crossings — all common on Colorado roads. They require extra attention and often a reduction in speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop in Colorado, two cars arrive at exactly the same time from opposite directions. One is going straight and one is turning left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The left-turning vehicle has the right of way,b:The vehicle going straight has the right of way,c:Both may proceed simultaneously since they are on opposite sides,d:The vehicle that arrived from the north always goes first
note: When two vehicles face each other at a 4-way stop, the vehicle going straight has the right of way over a turning vehicle. The left-turning vehicle must wait for the straight-going vehicle to clear the intersection before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in Colorado, at what speed should you enter a curve?
options: a:At the posted speed limit for the road,b:Slow enough before the curve so you can maintain a steady speed through it,c:Faster than the advisory speed on the curve warning sign,d:At highway speed — curves are rated for maximum vehicle capability
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve so you can travel through it at a steady, controlled speed. Braking in a curve shifts vehicle weight and reduces traction. Advisory speed signs on curves indicate a safe speed for the average driver under good conditions — in rain or ice, go slower.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when a school bus stops and activates its flashing red lights on a two-lane Colorado road?
options: a:Stop only if driving behind the bus,b:Slow to 20 mph and pass with caution,c:Stop in both directions at least 20 feet from the bus until lights stop flashing,d:Yield to children crossing, then proceed
note: Colorado law requires vehicles traveling in both directions on an undivided road to stop at least 20 feet from a school bus displaying flashing red lights. You may not proceed until the arm retracts and lights stop flashing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Colorado, what is the speed limit in a school zone when children are present?
options: a:15 mph,b:20 mph,c:25 mph,d:30 mph
note: Colorado school zones have a 20 mph limit when children are present or warning lights are flashing. Always reduce speed well before the zone begins and remain alert for children near the roadway at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are stopping on a Colorado freeway shoulder because of a mechanical problem. What should you do?
options: a:Stop as close to the traffic lanes as possible so other drivers can see you,b:Pull as far off the road as possible, turn on hazard lights, and place warning triangles if available,c:Stop anywhere and wait in the vehicle without activating hazard lights,d:Walk to the nearest exit for help immediately
note: Pull as far off the travel lanes as possible, activate hazard flashers immediately, and set out warning triangles or flares if available. Stay inside the vehicle with your seatbelt buckled — waiting in the vehicle is safer than standing on the shoulder in most situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Colorado's seatbelt law, which occupants must wear seatbelts?
options: a:Only the driver,b:Driver and all front-seat passengers,c:All occupants in the vehicle,d:Only passengers under age 16
note: Colorado requires all vehicle occupants — front and rear seats — to wear a seatbelt. Colorado has primary enforcement for front seat occupants, meaning officers can stop a vehicle solely for a seatbelt violation. Rear seat adults may be issued a secondary enforcement citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, who must yield?
options: a:The largest vehicle.,b:The car on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals. Always check carefully and be prepared to yield even if you have the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does the driver's left arm and hand extended downward signal mean?
options: a:Turn left.,b:Turn right.,c:Stop.
note: Hand signals are used when turn signals are not working or are hard to see. Left arm straight out means a left turn, left arm bent upward means a right turn, and left arm extended downward means the driver is slowing or stopping. Always give the signal in advance so other road users can react safely.

question: A driver with a BAC between which levels is presumed to be Driving While Ability is Impaired (DWAI) in Colorado?
options: a:0.03 and 0.05 percent,b:0.05 and 0.07 percent,c:0.07 and 0.09 percent,d:0.09 and 0.11 percent
note: In Colorado, a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.05% to less than 0.08% creates a presumption of Driving While Ability Impaired (DWAI). This means your driving is considered impaired even though it is below the 0.08% DUI per se limit. Any alcohol can affect judgment and reaction time, so the safest choice is not to drive after drinking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle when:
options: a:Approaching an intersection with a stop sign.,b:Where there is a red light.,c:When a traffic officer orders you to stop.,d:All of the above.
note: You must come to a complete stop at stop signs, at steady or flashing red traffic lights, and any time a traffic officer directs you to stop. Stopping fully before the crosswalk or stop line allows you to check for pedestrians and cross traffic and prevents entering the intersection unsafely.

question: How should drivers respond to a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Drive carefully without stopping.,b:Come to a complete stop, yield, and proceed when safe.,c:Merge to the right.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in or close to the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Drowsy drivers can:
options: a:Stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.,b:Drive so poorly that they may appear to be drunk.,c:Be made fully alert by drinking coffee.,d:Drive better than well-rested drivers.
note: Drowsy drivers often weave, react slowly, and make poor decisions, so their driving can resemble that of an impaired or drunk driver. Opening a window or turning up the radio may briefly make you feel more awake, but they do not restore alertness or make driving safe. Coffee may help a little, but it cannot fully overcome serious fatigue. The only safe solution for drowsiness is to rest before driving or stop and sleep.

question: Which factor does stopping distance NOT depend on?
options: a:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.,b:Your own reaction time.,c:The time of day.
note: Stopping distance is the total distance your vehicle travels from the moment you see a hazard until you come to a complete stop. It depends on your reaction time, your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, the road surface, and vehicle weight. The time of day by itself does not change how far it takes your vehicle to stop, even though nighttime can affect visibility and how quickly you notice hazards.

question: What is the effect of combining drugs with alcohol on driving risk?
options: a:Is no more dangerous than consuming alcohol by itself.,b:Increases the risk of causing a crash.,c:Lessens the effect of alcohol on your ability to drive.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) can increase impairment and the risk of a crash.

question: Pennant-shaped traffic signs typically indicate:
options: a:School zones.,b:No passing zones.,c:Speed limits.,d:Railroad crossings.
note: Pennant‑shaped signs are sideways triangles that point to the right and are placed on the left side of the road. They are used specifically to mark the beginning of a no passing zone. When you see this sign, you must not start to pass another vehicle and should stay in your lane until the no passing zone ends.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you, what should you do to help them pass safely?
options: a:Pull off the road to let them pass.,b:Stay in your lane, keep right, and maintain or slightly reduce your speed to allow safe passing.,c:Flash your lights to signal them to hurry.
note: When another vehicle is passing you, stay in your lane, keep to the right, and maintain a steady speed or slightly reduce your speed if needed so the other driver can pass and return to the lane safely. Do not speed up or signal them to hurry; that can create a dangerous situation. You only pull off the road if necessary for safety, not as a routine response to being passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you allowed to cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass another car.,b:To turn into a driveway.,c:To pass a slow-moving truck.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean you must not cross them to pass another vehicle. However, you may cross double solid yellow lines to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If a driver accumulates how many points in a 12-month period will the license be suspended?
options: a:Five points,b:Ten points,c:Twelve points,d:Eighteen points
note: In Colorado, adult drivers who accumulate 12 or more points in a 12‑month period are subject to license suspension. Points are assigned for traffic violations, and reaching the threshold within the specified time frame can trigger administrative action against your license.

question: If a HAWK pedestrian signal is solid red, what must drivers do?
options: a:Slow down and prepare to stop.,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop.
note: A HAWK (High‑Intensity Activated crossWalK) signal shows a solid red light to drivers when pedestrians are crossing. A solid red means you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to allow you to proceed and the crosswalk is clear.

question: What should you do if an aggressive driver is following you closely?
options: a:Make eye contact and stare as they pass.,b:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,c:Move out of the aggressive driver’s way when safe.
note: When an aggressive driver is tailgating or acting dangerously, the safest response is to avoid confrontation. Do not make eye contact or try to block them. Instead, when it is safe, change lanes or otherwise move out of their way and let them pass to reduce the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the red, you should:
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.,b:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.,c:Honk your horn to warn them.,d:Drive through carefully without stopping.
note: Even if you have a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the crosswalk or intersection, including those crossing against the signal. Slow down and stop if necessary so they can cross safely, and do not try to drive around or in front of them.

question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:
options: a:Speed up to put more distance between you and the tailgater.,b:Slam on your brakes briefly to warn the tailgater.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage the tailgater to pass.,d:Flash your lights repeatedly to signal them.
note: If another driver is following too closely, the safest response is to create space and let them go by. Signal early, change lanes when it is safe, or gradually slow down so the tailgater can pass. Never speed up, slam on your brakes, or aggressively signal them, because those actions can trigger a crash or road rage.

question: What may happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medications?
options: a:The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.,b:The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.,c:The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.
note: Alcohol can interact with many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines in a way that increases drowsiness, slows reaction time, and impairs judgment more than either substance alone. This combined effect can be unpredictable and dangerous when driving, so you should avoid mixing alcohol with any medication that can affect alertness.

question: Who is required by law to wear a fastened safety belt in a moving vehicle?
options: a:The driver only.,b:Passengers in the front seat only.,c:Children between the ages of 8 and 18 only.,d:The driver, front-seat passengers, and all children 8–15 regardless of seating position.
note: In Colorado, the law requires the driver and all front‑seat passengers to wear safety belts. In addition, all children ages 8 through 15 must be properly restrained in a seat belt or appropriate child restraint, no matter where they sit in the vehicle. Wearing seat belts greatly reduces the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.

question: When backing up your vehicle, what is the recommended technique?
options: a:Rely only on your mirrors.,b:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing.,c:Open your door to check behind the vehicle.
note: When backing up, place your right arm over the back of the passenger seat, turn your head and upper body, and look directly through the rear window while moving slowly. Use your mirrors and check all sides, but do not rely only on mirrors or cameras, and never open your door to look behind while the vehicle is moving.

question: What should you adjust first when getting into a vehicle to drive?
options: a:Your rearview mirror,b:Your seat,c:The steering wheel
note: Before driving, adjust your seat first so you can reach the pedals and controls comfortably and have a clear view of the road. Once your seating position is correct, adjust the steering wheel and mirrors to match that position so they provide the best control and visibility.

question: How should a lap belt fit?
options: a:Loose across your waist.,b:Buckled snugly low across your hip bones.,c:Tucked under the seat for comfort.
note: A lap belt should be worn low and snug across the hip bones and pelvis, not across the soft part of the stomach. This helps the belt hold your body against the stronger bones in a crash and reduces the risk of internal injuries.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.,b:Lowering your ability to focus on driving.,c:Decreasing your chances of an accident.,d:Improving reaction time.
note: Stress and strong emotions can distract you, narrow your attention, and slow your decision‑making. This lowers your ability to focus on driving tasks such as scanning, judging gaps, and reacting to hazards, which increases crash risk.

question: Which is not permitted for a passenger in a moving motor vehicle?
options: a:Have an opened alcohol container.,b:Sleep.,c:Use a cell phone.,d:Listen to music.
note: Open‑container laws generally prohibit passengers from possessing or drinking from an open alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public road. Even if the driver is sober, passengers may not have open alcohol in most situations.

question: When stopped by law enforcement for a traffic violation, what must the driver present?
options: a:Proof of registration.,b:Their license.,c:Proof of insurance.,d:All of the above.
note: When stopped by law enforcement, you must present your driver license and, when requested, proof of registration and insurance. Drivers are legally required to carry all three and show them to an officer upon request.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:The posted maximum speed limit.,b:A speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent for current conditions.,c:A speed that is safe for existing road, traffic, and weather conditions.,d:All of the above.
note: You must never drive faster than the posted speed limit, and you must also slow down whenever road, traffic, weather, or visibility conditions make the posted limit unsafe. The safe speed is the lower of the posted limit or the speed that is reasonable and prudent for current conditions.

question: When changing lanes you should NOT do which of the following?
options: a:Fail to check side and rearview mirrors and blind spots.,b:Signal your intentions.,c:Check for other drivers who may also be moving into the same lane.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors and blind spots, signal your intention, and make sure no one else is moving into the same lane. Failing to check mirrors and blind spots is unsafe and should never be done.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?
options: a:Drive out fast to merge smoothly with the traffic.,b:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.,c:Blow your horn to warn cars you are entering the roadway.
note: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you must yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway. Enter only when it is safe and without forcing others to slow or change lanes suddenly.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:
options: a:Sit in your car and wait for help without signaling.,b:Sound your horn at passing motorists to get attention.,c:Move well off the road if possible, turn on your hazard (four-way) flashers, and exit the vehicle only if and when it is safe.,d:Walk along the highway to find help.
note: If your car breaks down on a highway, move as far off the road as possible, preferably onto the shoulder, and turn on your hazard flashers so other drivers can see you. If it is safe, you may raise the hood or place warning devices behind your vehicle. Stay away from moving traffic and exit the vehicle only when it is safe to do so.

question: Crosswalks are:
options: a:Always indicated only by horizontal pavement markings.,b:Always indicated by vertical markings.,c:Present whether marked or unmarked and must be respected.,d:Always unmarked.
note: A crosswalk is the part of the roadway set aside for pedestrians to cross, and it exists at most intersections whether or not it is painted. Drivers must yield to pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks and stop behind the crosswalk line when required.

question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow for left turns, what does it mean?
options: a:You may turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You must come to a complete stop before turning.,c:You should merge into the lane indicated by the arrow before turning.
note: A flashing yellow left-turn arrow means you may turn left, but only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. The turn is not protected, so you must wait for a safe gap before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you take before changing lanes or passing on an interstate?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots.,b:Stop on the shoulder of the road if you are tired.,c:You should always use cruise control.
note: Before changing lanes or passing on an interstate, you must signal, check your mirrors, and quickly check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. This ensures you do not move into a space already occupied by another vehicle. Stopping on the shoulder is only for emergencies, and cruise control should never be treated as something you "always" use.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Turn into the middle lane.,b:Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.,c:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.
note: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your way, you must turn into the lane closest to the one you came from. For example, if you are turning left from the leftmost lane, you must enter the leftmost lane on the new road. This keeps traffic organized and prevents collisions with drivers turning from the opposite direction.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Is never used as a traffic signal.,b:Means you must stop and may not turn in the direction of the arrow while it is red.,c:Means drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped if you are in the lane controlled by that arrow. You may not turn in the direction of the arrow while it is red, unless signs specifically allow a turn on red after stopping and yielding. It functions like a steady red light for that specific turning movement.

question: You may cross solid yellow center lines:
options: a:To pass traffic moving in the same direction.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:Only to make a turn into or out of a driveway or side road.,d:At any time for passing.
note: A solid yellow center line generally means no passing. You may cross a solid yellow line only when turning left into or out of a driveway, alley, or side road, and only when it is safe and legal to do so. You may not cross it just to pass another vehicle.

question: What happens to your tires' effectiveness on a wet roadway as your speed increases?
options: a:They become less effective at clearing water and can lead to hydroplaning.,b:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: As speed increases on a wet roadway, your tires have less time to squeeze water out from under the tread. This reduces traction and can cause hydroplaning, where your tires ride on top of the water and lose contact with the road. Even good tires can hydroplane at high speeds in enough water.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane road you cannot pass safely unless:
options: a:You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,b:You are able to clearly see the road ahead.,c:Your vehicle is capable of the speed necessary to complete the pass.,d:All of the above.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road is only safe when all key conditions are met: you must clearly see far enough ahead, your vehicle must be able to accelerate and complete the pass promptly, and you must be able to return fully to your lane before meeting any oncoming traffic. If any of these conditions are missing, you should not attempt to pass.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the pavement, you should:
options: a:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.,b:Slow down by gently applying the brakes and steer back onto the pavement when safe.,c:Slam on your brakes immediately.,d:Speed up and swerve onto the pavement.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, keep calm and maintain control. Ease off the accelerator, slow down gradually, and avoid jerking the steering wheel or slamming on the brakes. Once your speed is reduced and the way is clear, gently steer back onto the pavement. Sudden steering or hard braking can cause a skid or rollover.

question: When passing a large truck or bus, what should drivers of smaller vehicles be prepared for?
options: a:Loud noises.,b:Excess air pollution.,c:Wind gusts produced by the large vehicle.,d:No effect on vehicle stability.
note: Large trucks and buses push and pull a lot of air as they move, creating wind gusts that can affect the stability of smaller vehicles, especially at higher speeds. When passing or being passed by a large vehicle, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be prepared to make small steering corrections to stay in your lane.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:Less dangerous.,b:No more or less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous because you can see less of the road ahead, it is harder to judge distances and speeds, and glare from headlights can temporarily reduce your vision. In addition, there is a higher chance of encountering drowsy or impaired drivers. At night you should slow down and increase following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a divided multilane highway, if you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle, you should:
options: a:Stop immediately where you are regardless of lanes.,b:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available.,c:Slow down, move to provide a clear path, and stop if necessary.,d:Speed up to stay out of its way.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren on, you must yield the right-of-way. On a divided multilane highway, safely slow down and move to the side or to another lane to create a clear path, then stop if needed. Never speed up to stay ahead of the emergency vehicle or block its route.

question: What does a solid black HAWK signal indicate to drivers?
options: a:Drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:Drivers may proceed past the crosswalk with caution.,c:Drivers should slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A HAWK (High-Intensity Activated crossWalK) signal stays dark when no pedestrian has activated it. A dark HAWK signal is treated like an uncontrolled intersection: drivers may proceed through the crosswalk but must do so carefully and be prepared to yield to any pedestrians who may be crossing.

question: What does a single dashed white line mean between lanes?
options: a:Drivers may pass or change lanes if it is safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Drivers are not allowed to pass.
note: A single dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Drivers may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, while checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling before moving.

question: If an approaching train is near enough or going fast enough to be a danger, you must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution across the tracks.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Cross the tracks if there is no ground-level light signal.,d:Weave through railroad gates if you are in a hurry.
note: If a train is close enough or moving fast enough to be a danger, you must not cross the tracks. Trains cannot stop quickly, and they always have the right-of-way. Wait until the train has completely passed, the tracks are clear in both directions, and any gates or signals indicate it is safe before crossing.

question: If you become too drowsy to focus while driving, the safest action is to:
options: a:Drink a large energy drink.,b:Open the windows and turn on the air conditioning.,c:Pull off the road and rest.,d:Continue driving slowly until help is found.
note: Drowsy driving is extremely dangerous because it slows your reaction time and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel. Opening windows or drinking caffeine may not keep you alert enough. If you feel too tired to drive safely, the safest choice is to pull off the road in a safe place and rest.

question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should:
options: a:Depend solely on road signs to find your way.,b:Plan your route in advance.,c:Rely only on general knowledge of the area.,d:Drive faster to avoid getting lost.
note: When driving to an unfamiliar area, planning your route in advance helps you avoid sudden lane changes, missed turns, and distracted driving. Review maps or GPS directions ahead of time and allow extra travel time so you can focus on the road and drive smoothly and safely.

question: What color are signs indicating areas of public recreation or cultural interest?
options: a:Red.,b:Brown.,c:Green.
note: Brown signs are used for parks, recreation areas, historic sites, and other cultural or recreational points of interest. When you see a brown sign, expect facilities or locations related to outdoor activities or cultural attractions.

question: What should you do to help prevent crashes with other road users?
options: a:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your vehicle.,b:Communicate with other road users using signals or horn when appropriate.,c:Drive only on side streets and back roads.
note: To help prevent crashes, you must clearly communicate your intentions to others. Use turn signals, brake lights, and your horn when necessary, and drive predictably so other road users can anticipate your actions and respond safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:Stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,b:May drive through the intersection if it is clear.,c:Must slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, but only if the intersection is clear. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to oncoming traffic when turning left, and enter the intersection at a safe speed.

question: Which is the safest way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Speed up as you enter and slow down as you exit.,b:Maintain the same speed throughout.,c:Slow down entering the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.
note: The safest way to drive through a curve is to slow down before you enter, then gently accelerate as you exit. Entering too fast can cause you to lose traction or drift out of your lane, while controlled acceleration out of the curve helps stabilize the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing from the right lane into the left lane on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Look in your rearview mirror only for traffic behind you.,b:Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot and signal your intention.,c:Turn on your directional signal and move left without looking.,d:Assume no one is beside you if your mirrors appear clear.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors, then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move. Signal your intention in advance and change lanes only when it is safe and clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left.,b:The driver on the right.,c:Either driver may continue without stopping.
note: At an open (uncontrolled) intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Rely solely on your mirrors.,b:Begin signaling only as you move into the next lane.,c:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes and glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.,d:Signal 500 feet before changing lanes in residential areas.
note: When changing lanes, you must signal in advance (about 100 feet in many areas), check your mirrors, and then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Never rely only on mirrors, and do not start signaling at the same time you move; other drivers need advance warning.

question: If a vehicle using high beams approaches, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:The center of the road.,b:Either side of the road.,c:The right side of the road.
note: When an oncoming vehicle’s high beams are shining in your eyes, look toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. This reduces glare while still letting you track your lane position safely until the vehicle passes.

question: In rainy driving conditions which headlights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: In rain, fog, or snow, use low beam headlights. High beams can reflect off moisture in the air and back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams improve your ability to see the road and help other drivers see you.

question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, you should:
options: a:Assume it is safe to cross once one train passes.,b:Always stop before every set of tracks.,c:Look for a second train on the other track after one passes before you proceed.,d:Drive faster to beat the next train.
note: At crossings with more than one track, after one train passes, always check carefully for a second train on the other track before you proceed. Another train may be approaching from either direction and can be hidden by the first train.

question: At a multi-track railroad crossing where you have stopped, what should you do after a train passes?
options: a:Go through as soon as the train passes.,b:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before proceeding.,c:Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
note: At multi-track crossings, a second train can come on another track right after the first one passes. Stay stopped until you can clearly see down all tracks in both directions and are sure no other train is coming before you proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you point your front wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Turn your wheels to the right.,c:Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
note: When parked facing downhill on a two-way street, turn the front wheels toward the curb or road edge. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll into the curb or away from traffic instead of rolling into the roadway.

question: Compared with smaller cars, larger vehicles generally have:
options: a:Larger blind spots.,b:No blind spots.,c:Smaller blind spots.
note: Larger vehicles such as trucks and large SUVs have bigger blind spots than smaller cars. Areas directly behind and along the sides may not be visible in the mirrors, so you should avoid lingering in those zones.

question: What single action most reduces your risk of serious injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Limit your driving to weekdays.,b:Wear your seat belt.,c:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
note: Wearing a properly adjusted seat belt greatly reduces your risk of being killed or seriously injured in a crash. It helps keep you inside the vehicle, spreads crash forces over stronger parts of your body, and works together with airbags.

question: How must license plates be displayed?
options: a:Fastened so they cannot swing.,b:Folded for storage when not needed.,c:Placed vertically instead of horizontally.
note: License plates must be securely fastened so they do not swing, mounted horizontally, clearly visible, and kept clean. This ensures that the plate can be easily read by law enforcement and other officials.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign you should:
options: a:Always come to a full stop regardless of other traffic.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or roadway you are entering.,c:Yield only to traffic approaching from the left.,d:Proceed at the same speed unless another vehicle is present.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. You must let traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection go first. If there is no conflicting traffic or pedestrians, you do not have to stop, but you must still approach with caution.

question: A person's ability to drive can be impaired by which of the following?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:Any medication (prescription or over-the-counter),c:Lack of sleep.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol, many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines, and being very tired can all slow your reactions and reduce your awareness and judgment. Because any of these can make driving unsafe, you must consider their effects before deciding to drive.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Firmly apply your brakes.,b:Take your foot off the gas.,c:Apply your parking brake.
note: On a slippery road, the first and safest action is to ease off the accelerator so the vehicle slows down gradually. If you need to slow more, brake gently and steadily to avoid skidding; sudden or hard braking can cause loss of control.

question: Which signal requires coming to a complete stop, yielding to cross traffic/pedestrians, then proceeding when clear?
options: a:Flashing yellow light.,b:Solid red light.,c:Flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, you must yield to any cross traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms judgment.,b:It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.,c:It harms both driving skills and judgment.
note: Alcohol reduces both your driving skills and your judgment. It slows reaction time, harms coordination and vision, and makes you more likely to take risks or misjudge situations, which greatly increases the chance of a crash.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Proceed slowly through the intersection.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.,c:Stop and then proceed when the way is clear.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped in the direction of the arrow until it changes to green or a green arrow, unless a sign specifically allows a turn on red. You may not proceed in the direction of a red arrow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with a working traffic signal, drivers should:
options: a:Always follow the traffic signal instead of the officer.,b:Follow the directions given by the officer.,c:Honk to get the officer’s attention.,d:Proceed only when the light allows it.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, their hand signals and instructions override traffic lights and signs. You must follow the officer’s directions even if they conflict with the traffic signal.

question: Which activities are common causes of distracted driving?
options: a:Changing a radio station or CD.,b:Talking or texting on a phone.,c:Eating, drinking, or smoking.,d:All of the above.
note: Distracted driving includes any activity that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving. Changing the radio, talking or texting on a phone, and eating, drinking, or smoking are all common causes of distraction and increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?
options: a:On the main road, just before the exit lane.,b:Once you see a toll booth.,c:Once you have moved into the exit lane.,d:Before entering the exit lane.
note: Maintain highway speed until you are safely in the exit lane, then slow down to the posted exit or ramp speed. Braking on the main travel lanes can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child in a front seat, especially with a rear-facing child seat.,b:Children are safest when properly restrained in the rear seat, away from active front airbags.,c:You should always make sure all passengers are using a seat belt or appropriate child restraint.,d:All of the above.
note: The driver is responsible for making sure everyone is properly restrained with seat belts or appropriate child safety seats. Children are safest in the rear seat, and a rear-facing infant seat must never be placed in front of an active airbag because the airbag can seriously injure the child.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving.,b:Following other vehicles too closely.,c:Excessive speed under the driving conditions.,d:Rare vehicle defects.
note: Inattentive or distracted driving is one of the most common causes of crashes. While speeding and following too closely are also frequent contributing factors, inattentive driving is broadly recognized as a leading cause of collisions.

question: How should you act when approaching the scene of an accident while driving?
options: a:Keep your attention on your driving.,b:Keep moving.,c:Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.
note: When you approach a crash scene, you should keep driving safely and avoid unnecessary stopping or distractions. However, if you are involved in the crash, or if emergency help has not yet arrived and you can safely assist, you must stop and provide help as required by law.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, how should you respond?
options: a:Flash your vehicle's lights to let them know they are wrong.,b:Call the police immediately.,c:Stay calm and move out of their way.
note: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, the safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and create space by slowing down or changing lanes when it is safe. Do not try to punish or confront the other driver, as that can escalate road rage and increase the risk of a crash.

question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway that slants to the left indicates:
options: a:The road ahead will be narrower.,b:An intersection is just ahead.,c:A construction area is ahead.,d:You will be required to turn left soon.
note: A solid white edge line that angles or slants toward the center of the road is a warning that the lane or roadway is about to become narrower. You should stay centered in your lane, reduce speed if needed, and be prepared for less space on the roadway.

question: What best ensures safety when you back your vehicle?
options: a:Honk your horn before shifting into reverse.,b:Walk around and check behind the vehicle before getting in.,c:Only check rearview mirrors after getting in.
note: Before backing, walk around your vehicle and check behind and around it for children, pedestrians, and objects that may be in your blind spots. After you get in, use your mirrors and look over your shoulder while backing slowly. Relying only on mirrors or the horn is not enough to ensure safety.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.,b:Never pass them under any circumstances.,c:Flash your lights at them to get their attention.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots along their sides and directly behind them. If you avoid driving right next to them for long periods and do not follow too closely, the driver is more likely to see you in their mirrors and can react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you enter freeway traffic from an on-ramp?
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.,b:Signal and enter the freeway; freeway traffic must yield.,c:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
note: When entering a freeway, you should use the on‑ramp to build up speed, signal, and look for a gap. Yield to traffic already on the freeway and merge at or near the speed of traffic so you blend smoothly without forcing others to brake suddenly.

question: When driving in bad weather, you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Increase your speed to pass hazards quickly.,c:Decrease your following distance.,d:Turn off headlights during heavy rain.
note: In bad weather, roads are more slippery and visibility is reduced, so it takes longer to see hazards and to stop. Slowing down and increasing your following distance gives you more time and space to react if the vehicle ahead brakes or skids.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Replace tires with bad tread.,b:Do not speed when the roads are wet.,c:Use tires with proper air pressure.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. The faster you drive on a wet surface, the more likely this is to occur. Driving at a safe, reduced speed on wet roads greatly lowers the risk of hydroplaning.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate quickly.,b:Watch for children walking along the side of the road.,c:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
note: Children getting on or off a school bus may cross the road or walk along the edge of the street and can be unpredictable. After the bus’s red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, proceed slowly and watch carefully for children near the roadway.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing without flashing signals or gates, you should:
options: a:Cross immediately and as quickly as possible.,b:Always stop before crossing.,c:Be prepared to yield to any approaching train.
note: At a railroad crossing without flashing lights or gates, you must slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and be ready to stop. Trains always have the right‑of‑way, so you must be prepared to yield and never enter the tracks unless you are sure you can completely clear them.

question: Which of the following does NOT promote safe night driving?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean.,b:Be aware that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.,c:Carry a flashlight inside your vehicle at all times.,d:Stare directly into oncoming headlights to adjust your vision.
note: Safe night driving depends on maximizing your ability to see and be seen. You should keep the windshield clean, understand that dark window tint reduces visibility at night, and use tools like a flashlight only when stopped and needed. You should never stare into oncoming headlights; instead, glance to the right edge of your lane to avoid glare and preserve your night vision.

question: A speed advisory sign attached to a curve means:
options: a:You should reduce speed below the advisory in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.,b:The sign has a triangular shape.,c:The sign is blue with black lettering.,d:You may ignore the advisory if you drive carefully.
note: A speed advisory sign on a curve shows a recommended maximum speed for that curve in good conditions, not a mandatory limit. In rain, snow, ice, or other poor conditions, you should slow down even more than the advisory speed so you have enough traction and time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill next to a curb, what should you do after setting the parking brake?
options: a:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,b:Keep the rear tires against the curb.,c:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will move back and the front of the wheel will contact the curb, helping stop the vehicle from rolling into traffic.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what should you do first?
options: a:Accelerate and steer back onto the road quickly.,b:Ease off the accelerator, slow down with your wheels off the pavement, then carefully steer back onto the road when it is safe.,c:Stop quickly.
note: If your right wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm and avoid sudden moves. Ease off the accelerator, keep steering straight and parallel to the road, and let the vehicle slow down with gentle braking if needed. Once you have control and there is a safe gap in traffic, carefully steer back onto the pavement. Do not jerk the wheel or brake hard, as that can cause you to lose control.

question: What is the appropriate action approaching a railroad crossing that has no active signals?
options: a:Always bring the car to a complete stop.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:All railroad crossings have signals so you will never encounter this situation.,d:Speed up and cross quickly.
note: At a railroad crossing without active signals, you must slow down, look and listen for trains, and be ready to stop. Only proceed when you are sure no train is coming and the tracks are clear. You are not required to always stop if there is no sign or signal requiring a stop and no train is approaching.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:
options: a:Know when it is safe to cross the street.,b:Stop at the curb before crossing.,c:Possibly run out into the street without looking.,d:Yield to vehicles at all times.
note: In areas where children are playing, you should assume they may act unpredictably and could run into the street without looking. Drive slowly, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop at any time, because children often do not judge traffic safely.

question: How are reversible lanes typically indicated?
options: a:Double broken yellow lines.,b:Overhead lane-use control signals only.,c:Single broken white line.
note: Reversible lanes are often marked by double broken yellow lines and controlled by overhead lane-use signals that show whether the lane is open to your direction of travel. Always obey the overhead signals; they tell you when you may use the lane and when it is closed or reserved for oncoming traffic.

question: If you are in a line of traffic crossing tracks with no signals or gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,b:You must ensure there is room for your vehicle to completely clear all tracks without stopping.,c:You have the right-of-way so you do not need to check for trains.,d:You may stop on the tracks if traffic is heavy.
note: When you are in a line of traffic approaching railroad tracks, you must be sure there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear all tracks before you start across. Never enter a crossing unless you can drive completely through without stopping; stopping on the tracks is extremely dangerous.

question: On which signal do you have the right-of-way to complete a left turn?
options: a:A flashing yellow arrow.,b:A green arrow pointing left.,c:A solid green light.,d:A flashing red light.
note: A green left arrow gives you a protected left turn, meaning oncoming traffic and pedestrians facing you should be stopped by a red light, so you have the right-of-way to turn. With a solid green light, you may turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians; you are not guaranteed the right-of-way.

question: As a pedestrian, which practice is recommended?
options: a:Always insist on the right-of-way over a vehicle when using a crosswalk.,b:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching and cannot safely stop.,c:Enter a crosswalk at any time because it is the driver’s responsibility to stop.
note: Pedestrians should never suddenly step into the path of a close‑approaching vehicle, even in a crosswalk. The safest practice is to wait until it is clear that approaching drivers have enough time and distance to see you and stop. While drivers are required to yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, pedestrians must still use caution and good judgment before entering the roadway.

question: If you must stop along the road at night, what should you do to remain visible?
options: a:Turn off all your lights.,b:Turn on your emergency flashers and keep low beam headlights on.,c:Use only your parking lights.
note: When you must stop along the road at night, you want your vehicle to be as visible as possible to avoid being hit. Turn on your emergency flashers so your vehicle stands out to approaching drivers, and keep your low beam headlights on so others can see you without being blinded by high beams.

question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?
options: a:Try to reach your destination before it arrives.,b:Continue driving and try to stay out of its way.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights and a siren approaches, you must yield the right‑of‑way. Safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed. If you are in an intersection, continue through it, then pull over to the right and stop as soon as it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an intersection displaying a flashing yellow light you should:
options: a:Stop and wait for the light to change.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Proceed through the intersection with caution.,d:Increase speed to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and proceed with extra caution. Be prepared to yield and watch carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards in or near the intersection.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign is used to:
options: a:Warn drivers of existing or possible hazards ahead.,b:Alert drivers to school zones.,c:Mark public recreation areas.,d:Indicate regulatory instructions like speed limits.
note: Diamond‑shaped signs are warning signs. They alert drivers to existing or potential hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, merging traffic, or pedestrian crossings, so you can adjust your driving in advance.

question: How should you check your blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,b:Turn your head and glance over your shoulder into the blind spot.,c:Use only the outside rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors, signal, and then quickly turn your head to glance over your shoulder into the lane you want to enter. This head check is the only way to be sure a vehicle or motorcycle is not hidden in your blind spot.

question: A flashing red traffic signal is equivalent to which traffic device?
options: a:A solid red light.,b:Stop sign.,c:Yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, look for cross traffic and pedestrians, then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe to go.

question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign:
options: a:Warns you about conditions on or near the road ahead.,b:Directs you to cities and towns ahead.,c:Tells you about traffic laws and regulations.,d:Marks the beginning of a parking zone.
note: Yellow and black diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or changes in road width, so you can slow down and drive with extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you pass your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving and use the next exit.,b:Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,d:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, stay calm and continue to the next exit. It is illegal and extremely dangerous to stop, back up, cut across lanes, or make a U-turn on the highway or ramp. Use the next exit and safely re-route to your destination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When they are on a road to your right and you have reached an unmarked intersection at the same time.,b:When entering a street from a garage, driveway, or alley.,c:Even with a green arrow, you must still yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.
note: When entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage, you must stop and yield to all cross traffic and pedestrians on the sidewalk. Vehicles already on the roadway have the right-of-way. At unmarked intersections, you generally yield to vehicles on your right, and a green arrow gives you the right-of-way for that protected movement (though you must still yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it acceptable to proceed through an intersection showing a yellow light?
options: a:If you are already inside the intersection when the light turns yellow, proceed carefully.,b:If there is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.,c:If pedestrians are crossing in the direction you are going.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should continue through carefully and clear the intersection. If you have not yet entered, you are expected to slow and stop if you can do so safely, rather than speeding up to beat the red.

question: If you are involved in a traffic accident, what is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Stop immediately.,b:Call the police.,c:Help the injured.,d:Leave the scene.
note: If you are involved in a collision, the law requires that you stop immediately at or near the scene. Once stopped and safe, you should protect the scene, call police or emergency services as needed, and give reasonable assistance to anyone injured. Leaving the scene is illegal and can result in serious penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The amount of space you need to cross traffic safely depends on:
options: a:Road and weather conditions and oncoming traffic.,b:Whether a stop sign is present.,c:Use of your turn signals.,d:The color of the vehicle you are driving.
note: To cross traffic safely, you must have enough time and space based on how fast other vehicles are coming and how far away they are, as well as road and weather conditions that affect traction and acceleration. Signs, turn signals, or vehicle color do not change the actual space you need to cross safely.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, fellow road users must allow for what characteristic of large vehicles?
options: a:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.,b:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
note: Large trucks and other heavy vehicles need a much longer distance to stop because of their size and weight. When driving near them, allow extra space, avoid cutting in front of them, and do not linger in their blind spots so they have enough room to slow or stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are impeding traffic by driving too slowly on a two-lane, two-way road, what should you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,c:Not let other cars pass your vehicle.
note: If you are driving well below the speed of traffic on a two-lane, two-way road and vehicles are stacking up behind you, you should safely pull off to the right when possible and let them pass. Blocking faster traffic or intentionally preventing others from passing is unsafe and can be illegal.

question: What do orange-colored traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Railroad crossing ahead.,b:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations.,c:A school zone ahead.
note: Orange signs are temporary warning signs used for construction, maintenance, and sometimes emergency operations. They alert drivers to changing road conditions, workers, lane shifts, or equipment on or near the roadway so you can slow down and proceed carefully.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Stop and wait for green.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Continue normally through the intersection at full speed.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and proceed with extra caution. Look for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards, and continue only when it is safe.

question: If you are followed by a fire engine that is not using its emergency signals, how should you drive?
options: a:Continue to drive in a normal manner.,b:Speed up to get out of its way.,c:Stop as quickly as possible.
note: Emergency vehicles only require you to yield or pull over when they are using their lights and/or siren. If a fire engine behind you is not using emergency signals, treat it like any other vehicle and continue driving normally while obeying all traffic laws.

question: What should you do when roads are slippery?
options: a:Drive the posted speed limit and be cautious.,b:Slow down.,c:Drive more quickly.
note: On slippery roads, such as in rain, snow, or ice, you should reduce your speed below the posted limit. Lower speed gives your tires more chance to grip the road and gives you more time to react if you start to slide.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should turn the steering wheel:
options: a:To keep the front wheels straight.,b:In the direction you want the vehicle to go (into the skid),c:In the opposite direction of the skid.,d:Sharply in either direction to correct quickly.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This is often described as steering into the skid. As the vehicle straightens out and you regain traction, gently adjust the wheel to keep traveling in your intended path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you approach a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Stop; you may turn right after yielding if no sign prohibits it.,b:Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.,c:Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
note: A steady red light always means stop before the crosswalk or limit line. After stopping, you may turn right on red unless a sign says otherwise, but you must first yield to pedestrians and all traffic with the right‑of‑way.

question: Where should you place your hands on the steering wheel for best control?
options: a:1 and 11 o'clock,b:2 and 10 o'clock,c:3 and 9 o'clock.
note: Placing your hands at about 9 and 3 o’clock on the steering wheel gives you better control, balance, and leverage, and it keeps your arms in a safer position if the airbag deploys.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, you should:
options: a:Honk your horn and turn off the engine immediately.,b:Turn on hazard lights and continue at the same speed.,c:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, and pull safely off the road as soon as possible.,d:Try to shift into neutral and coast to a stop in the travel lane.
note: If power steering fails, the vehicle will still steer but it will take much more effort. Hold the wheel firmly, slow down, signal, and carefully move off the road to a safe place to stop and get the problem checked.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, you should:
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb (to the left) and set the parking brake.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb and leave in gear.,d:Leave the wheels turned toward the road center.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll back and the front tire will rest against the curb, helping prevent it from rolling into traffic.

question: If you are taking an over-the-counter medication, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Read the labels and warnings on the drug.,b:Drink alcohol instead to ease symptoms.,c:Ignore any warnings and drive as usual.
note: Many over‑the‑counter medicines can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slowed reactions. Always read the label and warnings before driving, and ask a doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure whether it is safe to drive.

question: If a HAWK pedestrian signal is flashing yellow, what should drivers do?
options: a:Drivers may proceed with caution.,b:Drivers should come to a complete stop.,c:Drivers should slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A HAWK signal’s flashing yellow phase warns drivers that the beacon is activating. You should slow down and be prepared to stop for pedestrians who may be entering the crosswalk. You do not have to stop yet, but you must be ready to stop as the signal may change to solid yellow and then red.

question: Under which circumstances must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When directed to stop by a flagger.,b:When control is by a posted stop sign.,c:When flashing red signals and gates are operating.,d:All of the above.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing any time you are directed by a flagger, when there is a stop sign at the crossing, or when red lights are flashing and/or the gates are down or coming down. Never drive around lowered gates or try to beat a train; trains are much faster and take far longer to stop than a car.

question: Which of the following can impair your driving ability?
options: a:Allergy medicines, b:Marijuana, c:Cold remedies, d:All of the above
note: Allergy medicines, marijuana, and many cold remedies can make you drowsy, slow your reaction time, or affect your judgment. Even legal or over‑the‑counter drugs can impair your driving, so always read labels and follow medical advice before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should drivers take when preparing to turn left?
options: a:Move into the correct lane and signal well in advance.,b:Slow down gradually while checking your mirrors and blind spots.,c:Watch for oncoming vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians before turning.,d:All of the above.
note: When preparing to turn left, you should move into the correct left lane, signal well in advance, slow down smoothly while checking your mirrors, and watch carefully for oncoming vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians in the crosswalk. All of these steps are important for a safe left turn.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic at a school zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.,b:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing even if it differs.,c:Assume the guard is not authorized to direct traffic.
note: Crossing guards are authorized to direct traffic in school zones to protect children and other pedestrians. You must obey their signals and instructions, even if they differ from traffic lights or what other drivers are doing.

question: What do orange work zone signs indicate?
options: a:It is summer.,b:You must immediately stop and back up.,c:Road work or construction is ahead and you should use extra caution.
note: Orange signs are used for temporary work zones and construction areas. They warn that road work, lane shifts, equipment, or workers may be present, so you should slow down, stay alert, and be prepared for unexpected or less‑than‑ideal driving conditions.

question: What are potential risks of worn or bald tires?
options: a:Are likely to hydroplane.,b:Can make turning more difficult.,c:All of the above.
note: Worn or bald tires have very little tread, which reduces traction with the road. This makes it harder for your tires to grip the pavement, so your stopping distance increases, your ability to steer and turn safely is reduced, and your risk of hydroplaning on wet roads goes up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, when should you return to the right lane?
options: a:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.,b:Return to the driving lane when there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,c:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.
note: After you pass on a two‑lane road, you should not cut back in too soon. Wait until you can see enough space between your vehicle and the one you passed—often when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror—then signal and return to the right lane.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn as a warning?
options: a:When passing a bicyclist.,b:When you see a child about to run into the street.,c:When traveling through an intersection.
note: Use your horn to alert others when there is a potential collision and you think they may not see you, such as when a child is about to run into the street. Avoid using the horn without a safety reason, like just to express frustration or to move traffic along.

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
