options: a:Because the bicyclist may need to swerve or change position to avoid hazards.,b:Because bicycles are smaller and harder to see, especially at intersections and driveways.,c:Because oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass, and you must leave extra space for the bicyclist.
note: When passing a bicycle, you must allow plenty of space because the cyclist may need to swerve to avoid potholes or debris, and oncoming drivers may not see you move into their lane. Always check for oncoming traffic, signal, and give the bicyclist a safe clearance as required by your state’s minimum passing distance law.

question: Which statement about passing motorcycles is true?
options: a:It is okay for drivers of other vehicles to follow motorcycles closely.,b:A motorcycle with two people on it is more balanced than one with one rider.,c:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,d:Motorcycles are not entitled to a full lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane, just like any other vehicle. When you pass a motorcycle, you should move completely into the adjacent lane, just as you would when passing a car or truck. Never crowd a motorcycle in the same lane or follow too closely, because they can stop and maneuver more quickly than larger vehicles.

question: What is the best long-term method to avoid hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep tires properly maintained with good tread.,b:Watch out for standing water but take no other actions.,c:Use cruise control in wet or slushy conditions.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water instead of gripping the road. The best long‑term way to reduce this risk is to keep your tires in good condition with proper tread depth and correct air pressure. In wet conditions you should also slow down and avoid using cruise control so you can respond quickly if the vehicle starts to lose traction.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.,b:When exiting an expressway only.,c:When following a motorcycle only.
note: You should increase your following distance whenever conditions make it harder to see, stop, or react in time. This includes driving behind large vehicles that block your view, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when following motorcycles or bicycles, or when being tailgated. More space gives you extra time to avoid sudden hazards.

question: Which statement best describes stopping in a travel lane?
options: a:You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong entrance ramp of the freeway.,b:You may stop to drop off passengers.,c:You should not stop in a travel lane for any reason.,d:You may stop to look up an address.
note: You must not stop in a travel lane because you can be hit from behind or cause sudden lane changes by other drivers. If you miss an exit or need to check directions, continue driving until you can safely pull off the road or reach the next exit. Never back up, make a U‑turn on a freeway ramp, or stop in a lane just to drop off passengers or look for an address.

question: Signs that warn drivers about hazardous conditions are called what?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potential hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or merging traffic. They are usually yellow or fluorescent yellow‑green with black symbols or lettering, and they give you time to slow down or adjust your driving before you reach the hazard.

question: Drivers who have been drinking before driving:
options: a:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,b:Do not have sufficient control of their body, mind, or vehicle.,c:Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain and body functions. Even small amounts reduce judgment, coordination, and reaction time, so a driver who has been drinking does not have full control of their body, mind, or vehicle. This makes driving unsafe and greatly increases crash risk.

question: What is the proper response to a tire blowout while driving?
options: a:Do not immediately use your brakes.,b:Gradually slow down and pull off the road.,c:Take your foot off the gas.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly and do NOT slam on the brakes. First, take your foot off the gas and let the vehicle slow down gradually while you keep it going straight. Once you have the car under control and your speed has dropped, gently brake as needed and steer to the side of the road to stop in a safe place.

question: What type of markings or symbols are used on some highways to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?
options: a:Arrows painted on lanes or posted on signs.,b:Flashing red lights over each lane.,c:White lines on the side of the road only.
note: On many roads and highways, arrows are painted directly in the lanes and shown on overhead or roadside signs to indicate which lanes are for turning and which are for going straight. Drivers must follow these lane-use arrows to be in the correct lane before turning or proceeding through an intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, you must:
options: a:Slow down until it has passed.,b:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass.,c:Drive to the right-hand edge of the road and stop until it passes.,d:Keep driving and maintain your lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and/or flashing lights, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping until it has passed. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull to the right and stop. This creates a clear path so emergency responders can get through quickly and safely.

question: What may happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both the alcohol and drug may be increased.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both may be reduced.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs, including many prescription or over-the-counter medicines, can intensify or unpredictably change the effects of both substances. This can greatly increase drowsiness, confusion, poor judgment, and slowed reactions, making driving extremely dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following statements about passing is true?
options: a:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,b:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes or passing.,c:Wait until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.,d:All of the above.
note: When passing, you must signal early (at least 100 feet before changing lanes), check your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to clear your blind spot, and only move back into your original lane when you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle, including both headlights, in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a crowded freeway, what should you do to merge into traffic?
options: a:Use your side and rearview mirrors and check blind spots, b:Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic, c:Yield to traffic already on the freeway, d:All of the above.
note: When entering a crowded freeway, use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, check your mirrors and blind spots carefully, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Merge only when there is a safe gap so you do not force other drivers to brake suddenly.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember trucks generally:
options: a:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.,b:Require less distance to stop on a downgrade.,c:Have smaller blind spots than cars.,d:Require no additional space when turning.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need more distance to stop and more room to maneuver. Never cut closely in front of a truck, and allow extra following distance so the truck has enough space to slow or stop safely.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a turn-control signal mean?
options: a:Means that drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.,b:Has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light for that turn movement: the protected turn is ending and you should prepare to stop if safe.,c:Is never used as a traffic signal.
note: A solid yellow arrow warns that your protected turning movement is ending and the signal is about to change. It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light for that direction: the green arrow is ending, and you should prepare to stop if it is safe to do so. If you are already in the intersection and cannot stop safely, you should complete the turn with caution.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, how should you pass a bicyclist traveling the same direction?
options: a:Do not pass until you come to a traffic signal or stop sign.,b:Slow down and wait until there is no opposing traffic, then pass with sufficient space.,c:Continue driving straight; it's the bicyclist’s responsibility to get out of your way.
note: On a two-lane road without a bike lane, treat a bicyclist like a slow-moving vehicle. Slow down, wait until there is no oncoming traffic, then move over and pass with plenty of clearance—typically at least 3 feet, or more at higher speeds—only when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: What is the 'No zone' in relation to large trucks and buses?
options: a:The area of blind spots around a truck or bus.,b:A reduced speed zone near trucks.,c:A lane reserved for large vehicles only.
note: The No-Zone is the large blind-spot area around trucks and buses where the driver cannot easily see other vehicles. Staying out of these areas, especially along the sides, directly behind, and close in front of the truck, helps avoid collisions because the truck driver may not know you are there.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:Either one.,b:The vehicle on the left.,c:The vehicle on the right.,d:The vehicle that arrived first.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals controlling the intersection.

question: When sharing the road with large trucks, drivers should know that trucks:
options: a:Have large blind spots and require extra room to maneuver and stop.,b:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger cars.,d:Have a smaller turning radius than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots along the sides, behind, and sometimes directly in front of them. Because of their size and weight, they also need more distance to stop and more space to turn or change lanes. Giving trucks extra room and avoiding their blind spots improves safety for everyone.

question: Which greatly increases stopping distances and the severity of crashes?
options: a:High speeds,b:Slow speeds,c:Night driving,d:Driving in neutral
note: As speed increases, your stopping distance grows much faster than your speed, and any crash will be more severe because impact forces are higher. Driving at a safe speed for conditions gives you more time and space to react and reduces the seriousness of collisions.

question: If you see an animal on the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, be prepared to stop, and pass cautiously only when safe.,b:No special action is required.,c:Speed up to pass the animal quickly.
note: When you see an animal on or near the road, slow down, be prepared to stop, and pass very cautiously only when it is safe. Sudden swerving can cause you to lose control or hit another vehicle, so focus on controlling your speed and giving the animal space while watching for others that may follow.

question: Why must you use extra caution around a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:They may be deaf.,b:They are blind and may not see traffic.,c:They are crossing illegally.
note: A white cane or guide dog identifies a pedestrian as blind or visually impaired. They may not see you or judge your speed, so you must slow down, be prepared to stop, and always yield the right‑of‑way to them.

question: How should you handle turns on slick roads?
options: a:Change lanes quickly to avoid hazards.,b:Accelerate quickly before entering the turn.,c:Take turns more slowly than usual.
note: On slick or slippery roads, turns must be taken more slowly than usual. Reducing speed before the turn helps prevent skidding and loss of control, because your tires have less traction on wet, icy, or loose surfaces.

question: Before passing another vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots.,b:Honk your horn at least three times.,c:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,d:Flash your headlights repeatedly.
note: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots to be sure the lane is clear, then signal and move over only when it is safe. After passing, return to your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, leaving plenty of space.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, what must you do?
options: a:Keep driving in your lane.,b:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop.,d:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights or siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right as possible and stopping. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs otherwise.

question: What should drivers do when approaching a traffic signal showing a steady yellow arrow?
options: a:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,b:Should stop if it is safe to do so.,c:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,d:Proceed as if the arrow were green.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected movement is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. You should stop if you can do so safely before the intersection. If you are already in the intersection and cannot stop safely, complete your turn with caution.

question: At a light rail crossing, what must you always do?
options: a:Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.,b:Look both ways before crossing tracks and obey all traffic signals.,c:Drive around lowered gates if you can get through quickly.
note: At light rail crossings, you must always look carefully in both directions for approaching trains and obey all warning signs, signals, and gates. Trains can be quiet and may come from either direction, so you must never drive around lowered gates or ignore flashing lights, even if you do not see a train.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light tell you to do?
options: a:Merging traffic.,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Pedestrian crossing.
note: A flashing yellow traffic light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in or entering the intersection.

question: Many crashes are caused by which of the following?
options: a:Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.,b:Drivers consistently checking their mirrors and blind spots.,c:Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
note: Driving too fast for conditions is a major cause of crashes. Even if you are under the posted speed limit, you must slow down when roads are wet, icy, congested, or visibility is reduced. Safe speed is always based on current conditions, not just the posted limit.

question: On what road surfaces does your stopping distance increase?
options: a:On wet or icy roads.,b:On paved highways in perfect conditions.,c:Only when driving during the day.
note: Stopping distance increases on any surface that reduces traction, such as wet, icy, snowy, or gravel roads. On these surfaces, your tires grip the road less effectively, so you need more distance to stop. Reduce your speed and leave extra following distance in poor conditions.

question: If you are driving in another vehicle's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Keep a steady pace.,b:Stay in the driver's blind spot.,c:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
note: Blind spots are areas alongside and slightly behind a vehicle that the driver cannot see in their mirrors. If you are driving in another vehicle’s blind spot, you should either move ahead or drop back so the driver can see you. Staying out of blind spots reduces the risk of being sideswiped or cut off.

question: Your vehicle's brake lights tell other drivers that you are:
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Making a turn.,c:Using your emergency brake.,d:Slowing down or stopping.
note: Brake lights are designed to warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping. This gives them time to react and reduce speed safely. They do not indicate lane changes, turns, or use of the parking/emergency brake.

question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Cancels the effect of alcohol.,b:Decreases BAC.,c:Has no effect on BAC.
note: Coffee, fresh air, or other remedies do not reduce BAC; only time will metabolize alcohol out of your system.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Just before changing lanes, which check should you perform?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles in your blind spot.,b:Check only the side view mirror.,c:Check the rearview mirror only.
note: Before changing lanes, first check your mirrors to see traffic around you, then quickly turn your head to look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change. This head check lets you see the blind spot that mirrors cannot show, helping you avoid vehicles hidden beside you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Sound your horn to alert other drivers.,b:Check rearview and side mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots.,c:Turn on your headlights to indicate a lane change.
note: On a multilane highway, prepare for a lane change by checking your rearview and side mirrors, then looking over your shoulder to check your blind spot. After you are sure the lane is clear, signal, and then move over smoothly when it is safe.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Turn off the ignition and carefully pull off the road.,c:Blow your horn.
note: If your accelerator sticks, shift to neutral if possible, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, and steer toward the side of the road. Once you are in control and moving to a safe place, turn the ignition off without locking the steering, and brake gently to a stop off the roadway.

question: Why must drivers be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:Motorcycles are more difficult to see than cars.,b:Motorcyclists do not have the same rights as other vehicles.,c:Motorcyclists rarely use headlights.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and narrower than cars, so they are easier to overlook in mirrors and blind spots and harder to judge for speed and distance. Because of this, drivers must look carefully for motorcycles, give them a full lane, and use extra caution when turning or changing lanes.

question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Yes.,b:No.,c:Only if there is no oncoming traffic.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means you may not cross the lines to pass another vehicle in either direction. You may only cross to make a permitted left turn, such as into or out of a driveway or side road, when it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver's left arm extended upward is a hand signal for:
options: a:Turning left.,b:Coming to a stop.,c:Turning right.
note: Standard hand signals use the left arm: straight out for a left turn, bent upward at the elbow for a right turn, and bent downward for slowing or stopping. A left arm extended upward tells you the driver intends to turn right.

question: How should you apply the gas pedal for smooth acceleration?
options: a:Gradually and smoothly.,b:By tapping rapidly for quick bursts.,c:As quickly as possible to merge with traffic.
note: For smooth, controlled acceleration, press the gas pedal gradually and smoothly using the ball of your foot while keeping your heel on the floor. This helps you avoid sudden speed changes, maintain traction, and keep better control of the vehicle.

question: Under what circumstances may you drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:As long as you are not the driver.,b:Never; it is illegal to consume or possess an open container in the passenger area on a public road in a standard passenger vehicle.,c:If you are riding in the back seat.,d:If you are riding in the back of a pickup truck.
note: Open container laws generally prohibit drinking alcohol or having an open alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public road, even if you are not the driver. Some states allow limited exceptions (such as certain hired vehicles or living quarters of RVs), but for test purposes you should treat drinking alcohol in any part of a passenger vehicle on a public highway as illegal.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to avoid it.,b:Stop immediately and block its path.,c:Make every effort to give it a clear path of travel (pull over if safe).
note: If safe, pull to the side and yield to emergency vehicles so they can pass or reach their destination quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a Merging traffic sign on the freeway, what should you do if traffic is present beside you?
options: a:Always remain at your present speed.,b:Honk at incoming traffic.,c:Make room for entering vehicles if possible.
note: When safe, move over or adjust your speed to make room for merging traffic; if no vehicle is beside you, you may move over a lane.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage determine how much it impairs you?
options: a:Beer is less impairing than wine.,b:Effects depend on the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream, not the beverage type.,c:Hard ciders and mixed drinks are most impairing.
note: Impairment depends on the amount of alcohol consumed and blood alcohol concentration, not the specific type of beverage.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing and you neither see nor hear a train, when must you stop?
options: a:If a stop sign is posted.,b:If a crossing gate is lowered.,c:If the crossing lights are flashing.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing whenever a stop sign is posted, the lights are flashing, the gate is down, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is approaching. Even if you do not see or hear a train, a posted stop sign still requires a complete stop before you proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have the right-of-way at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Assume other drivers will obey right-of-way rules and proceed without looking.,b:Take extra time to check for crossing traffic and bicyclists before moving.,c:Wave other drivers forward before proceeding.,d:Immediately accelerate through the intersection.
note: Even with the right-of-way, always check for other vehicles and pedestrians before entering an intersection to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When the centerline on your side is a broken yellow line and it is safe to do so.,b:When in a curve or on a hill because you are unlikely to meet oncoming traffic.,c:By using the shoulder of the roadway.
note: Passing is only allowed where pavement markings permit it and when you have enough clear space to pass safely. A broken yellow line on your side of the centerline means you may pass if there is no oncoming traffic and you can complete the maneuver without speeding or cutting off other vehicles. You must never pass on hills, curves, or by driving on the shoulder.

question: Two solid white lines painted across a traffic lane mark what and how should drivers respond?
options: a:They mark a stop line at an intersection; stop before the line when required and yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk.,b:They show crosswalk boundaries; yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.,c:They indicate no one has right-of-way.
note: Two solid white lines painted across a lane at an intersection usually mark a stop line, often associated with a crosswalk. The crosswalk itself is typically marked by two parallel white lines or a series of white stripes. Drivers must stop before the stop line when required and must always yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: To cross railroad tracks safely, what should you do?
options: a:Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.,b:Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if it is safe to do so.,c:Cross quickly when a train is approaching.,d:Rely on other drivers to signal whether it is safe.
note: At railroad crossings, always slow down, listen, and look carefully in both directions for trains. Obey all warning signs, lights, and gates. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely without stopping.

question: Which of the following is a telltale sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.,b:Weaving between lanes.,c:Making quick and sudden stops.,d:Driving with headlights off.
note: Impaired drivers often show several warning behaviors, including driving much slower than surrounding traffic, weaving or drifting between lanes, making sudden or jerky stops, and sometimes driving without headlights at night. Any of these can be a telltale sign of a drunk or impaired driver.

question: Crossbuck signs indicate:
options: a:Railroad crossings.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.,d:Pedestrian crossings.
note: A crossbuck sign is the white X-shaped sign found at railroad crossings. It warns that you are approaching train tracks and must yield to any approaching train, stopping if a train is near or warning devices are active.

question: Regulatory signs are used to:
options: a:Warn about possible hazards.,b:Provide directions to cities and towns.,c:Indicate what a driver must or must not do.,d:Give distance to the next exit.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do under the law, such as speed limits, stop, yield, or turn restrictions. They are different from warning signs (hazards) and guide signs (directions and distances).

question: When driving at night and another vehicle is approaching, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:High beams.,b:Low beams.,c:Parking lights only.
note: When another vehicle is approaching at night, you must use low beams so you do not blind the oncoming driver. High beams are only for use when there is no oncoming traffic and you are not following another vehicle closely.

question: It is best to keep a space cushion:
options: a:Only behind your vehicle.,b:Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.,c:Only in front of your vehicle.,d:On all sides of your vehicle.
note: A space cushion is the open space around your vehicle that gives you time to react. You should keep space in front, behind, and to both sides whenever possible so you can steer or brake to avoid hazards.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the line dividing your lane from the lane you wish to enter is which type of line?
options: a:Double solid yellow,line not crossable.,b:Broken white,line that separates lanes traveling in same direction.,c:Solid yellow,line you must not cross.,d:Broken yellow,line dividing opposing traffic.
note: You may pass another vehicle only when the line on your side is broken and it is safe. A broken yellow line between lanes of opposing traffic allows passing when clear. Solid yellow lines mean no passing, and white lines separate traffic moving in the same direction, not opposing lanes.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer need to stop from 55 mph?
options: a:125 feet,b:50 feet,c:400 feet.
note: A fully loaded tractor‑trailer needs much more distance to stop than a car. At about 55 mph, it can take roughly 400 feet or more to come to a complete stop, so you should never cut closely in front of a large truck.

question: A traffic light showing a green arrow with a red light means:
options: a:You may go straight in any direction.,b:You may only move in the direction the green arrow indicates and only if the way is clear.,c:You must wait for a solid green light to go in that direction.,d:You may turn left without yielding to pedestrians.
note: A green arrow means you are allowed to move only in the direction the arrow points, and only if the path is clear. The red light still applies to all other movements, so you may not go straight or turn in other directions. You must still yield to pedestrians and any traffic already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection and are not in the proper lane to turn, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,c:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.
note: If you are not in the correct lane to make a turn, you should continue straight and go to the next intersection, then make your turn from the proper lane. Sudden lane changes or turning from the wrong lane can surprise other drivers and cause crashes.

question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:
options: a:Must always be obeyed.,b:Are merely suggestions.,c:Must be followed only when other traffic is present.,d:Apply only to commercial vehicles.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls, not suggestions. They must be obeyed at all times because they regulate speed, direction, and right‑of‑way to keep traffic safe and orderly.

question: Which statement about yielding to emergency vehicles is correct?
options: a:May follow each other.,b:May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.,c:Have the right-of-way when using sirens and/or flashing lights.
note: When an emergency vehicle is using its siren and/or flashing lights, you must yield the right‑of‑way. Safely pull over to the right and stop, or follow any lawful instructions given by the emergency personnel, so they can pass quickly and safely.

question: When a vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) starts to lose traction, drivers should:
options: a:Pump the brakes manually.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer out of danger.,c:Release the brake immediately.,d:Shift to neutral and coast.
note: With ABS, you should press the brake pedal firmly and hold it while steering where you want to go. The ABS system automatically pumps the brakes to help prevent wheel lockup, so you can maintain steering control and avoid the hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make the turn quickly from your lane of travel.,b:Stop and back up.,c:Continue to the next exit or safe location to turn around.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, stay calm and continue driving to the next exit or another safe place to turn around. Never stop, swerve suddenly, or back up on the freeway or shoulder, because traffic is moving at high speeds and unexpected stopping or reversing can cause serious crashes.

question: How does increasing speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It increases your field of vision.,b:It decreases your field of vision.,c:It makes it easier to see cross traffic.
note: As your speed increases, your field of vision narrows. You see less to the sides (your peripheral vision shrinks), which makes it harder to detect pedestrians, cross traffic, and hazards at the edges of the road. This is why high speeds require extra caution and looking farther ahead.

question: Traffic may NOT pass from either direction over which centerline marking?
options: a:A single broken yellow line.,b:A combination solid and broken yellow line.,c:Double solid yellow lines.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing for traffic in either direction. You may not cross them to pass another vehicle. You may usually cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

question: What should you do when approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians or other vehicles already in the intersection and be ready for unexpected hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you reach an intersection controlled by a flashing red light?
options: a:Stop and wait for a flashing green light.,b:Come to a full stop and proceed only when the way is clear.,c:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,d:Yield to oncoming traffic but do not stop.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals fail, you should use which method to indicate turns?
options: a:Your horn.,b:Your headlights.,c:Hand signals.,d:Tail lights only.
note: If your electrical turn signals are not working, you must use standard hand and arm signals to show other drivers when you intend to turn or stop. Extend your left arm straight out for a left turn, bend your left arm up at the elbow for a right turn, and bend your left arm down for slowing or stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What moves are allowed from a center lane marked for two-way left turns?
options: a:You may pass slow-moving traffic.,b:You may make left turns.,c:You may make U-turns.
note: A center lane marked for two‑way left turns is only for making left turns (and U‑turns where they are specifically legal), not for passing or driving straight through. You enter this lane briefly to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road, then leave it as soon as it is safe.

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) depends on each of the following except:
options: a:How much you drink.,b:How much time passes between drinks.,c:Your body weight.,d:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.
note: Your BAC is determined by how much alcohol you consume, how quickly you drink it, and factors like your body weight and sex. The type of drink (beer, wine, liquor) does not matter by itself—what matters is the total amount of pure alcohol you take in over time.

question: How should head restraints be positioned for safety?
options: a:Removed from the seats if possible.,b:Adjusted so the top is about level with the top of your ears and close to the back of your head.,c:Adjusted to sit well above the head.
note: Head restraints should be adjusted so the top is roughly level with the top of your ears and as close to the back of your head as possible. Proper contact with the back of your head helps reduce whiplash injuries in a rear‑end collision.

question: If you are involved in an accident, which of the following actions should you take at the scene?
options: a:Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.,b:Turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles.,c:Avoid standing in traffic lanes.,d:All of the above.
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop at or near the scene, then, if it is safe, move vehicles out of traffic, turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles to reduce fire risk, and stay out of traffic lanes. All of these steps help prevent additional collisions and injuries.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you must:
options: a:Leave a note with your name, address, and the circumstances of the accident.,b:Drive away if damage appears minor.,c:Wait until the police arrive before leaving any information.,d:Do nothing unless someone witnessed the accident.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you must stop and leave a written note in a secure, visible place on the vehicle with your name, address, and an explanation of what happened. In many states you must also report the collision to law enforcement, especially if the damage is significant.

question: If nearby drivers are reacting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Do not make eye contact, avoid gestures, and calmly create space between you and them.,b:Try to engage with them to resolve the issue.,c:Speed up to get away from them quickly.
note: When other drivers are angry or aggressive, your goal is to avoid escalating the situation and to protect yourself. Do not make eye contact, do not respond with gestures or yelling, and do not race or challenge them. Instead, stay calm and create space by slowing slightly, changing lanes, or exiting or pulling over in a safe, public place if needed.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:They are not important and can be ignored.,b:They are only used in construction zones.,c:They provide important information, warnings, and guidance that drivers must obey.
note: Pavement markings are a key part of the traffic control system. They tell you where you may drive, pass, or stop; indicate lane use; show where turning is allowed; and warn of conditions such as no‑passing zones, crosswalks, and stop lines. You must obey pavement markings just like signs and signals.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what is the safest way to return to the road?
options: a:Ease off the gas, slow down, and very carefully steer back onto the pavement when it is safe.,b:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Stop your car immediately on the edge of the road, even if it is not safe to do so.,d:Accelerate back onto the pavement immediately.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, do not jerk the wheel or brake hard. First, ease off the accelerator and let the car slow down while you keep a firm grip on the steering wheel. When your speed is under control and the shoulder is stable, gently steer back onto the pavement with small, smooth movements so you don’t lose control or skid.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Brake hard immediately.,b:Maintain your speed and continue driving normally.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle straight, and gradually slow by easing off the gas before pulling off the road safely.
note: When a tire blows out, the sudden loss of air can cause your vehicle to pull to one side. Grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle going straight. Do not slam on the brakes; instead, ease off the accelerator and let the car slow down gradually. Once you have control and your speed has dropped, steer to a safe place off the road and brake gently to stop.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, which action should you take?
options: a:Cross especially quickly when a train is approaching.,b:Look for a train.,c:Slow down only if lights are flashing.,d:Ignore warning gates and continue.
note: When approaching any railroad crossing, you must look and listen for trains and be prepared to stop. If warning lights are flashing, gates are down, or a train is clearly approaching, you must stop and remain stopped until it is safe and legal to proceed.

question: What plates are required on Colorado motor vehicles?
options: a:A plate only on the rear.,b:Plates on both the front and back of the vehicle.,c:A plate only on the front.
note: Colorado law requires most motor vehicles to display license plates on both the front and rear of the vehicle so they can be identified from either direction.

question: Which statement about work zones is true?
options: a:May be moving or stationary.,b:Is marked with black and white signs.,c:Does not require a driver to slow down and pay extra attention.
note: Work zones can be either stationary (such as a fixed construction area) or moving (such as striping or maintenance vehicles). They are usually marked with orange signs, and drivers must slow down, obey posted work-zone speeds, and pay extra attention for workers and equipment.

question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:
options: a:A circular green sign.,b:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,c:A reflective orange triangle.,d:A rectangular red sign.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle, often bordered with red, mounted on the rear of vehicles that travel 25 mph or less. When you see this emblem, reduce speed and be prepared to slow down or pass only when it is safe and legal.

question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to prevent the pass.,b:Go the same speed.,c:Slow down to give room in front of your vehicle for the pass.
note: If a driver behind you wants to pass, you should help them do it safely. Maintain a steady path and, if needed, slightly slow down to create more space in front of your vehicle so the passing driver has room to move back into the lane without cutting too closely in front of you.

question: What color pavement markings separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Both yellow and white
note: Yellow lines on the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction or mark the right edge of the roadway.

question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving skills?
options: a:Only a BAC above the legal limit will impair concentration and judgment.,b:Alcohol does not affect driving.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can impair concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.
note: Any amount of alcohol can begin to affect the brain, reducing concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. You can be unsafe to drive even before reaching the legal BAC limit.

question: What should your inside rearview mirror show after adjustment?
options: a:The passengers in the backseat.,b:Your own reflection.,c:The entire rear window.
note: The inside rearview mirror should be adjusted so you can see the entire rear window while sitting in your normal driving position, without moving your head. This maximizes your view of traffic behind you.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.,b:Allow the motorcycle to use only half a lane.,c:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other motor vehicle. Never try to share a lane with a motorcycle or crowd them; give them the full lane width for safe maneuvering.

question: Which of these is a common effect of alcohol on a driver?
options: a:Improved judgment.,b:Poor coordination.,c:Increased alertness.
note: Alcohol commonly causes poor coordination, slower reaction time, and reduced judgment. These effects make it harder to steer, brake, and respond safely to traffic situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn, your vehicle should be positioned:
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Close to the left side of the street.,c:As close as possible to the right side of the street.,d:In the middle of the intersection.
note: For a right turn, you should be in the lane closest to the right curb or edge of the roadway, and as close to the right side of that lane as is safe and legal. This positioning shortens the turn, reduces conflicts with other traffic, and helps keep you in your proper lane as you complete the turn.

question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection indicate?
options: a:Always come to a full stop at the intersection.,b:Yield to vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.,c:Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
note: A red and white triangle is a yield sign. You must slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary, yielding the right-of-way to any vehicles or pedestrians already in or close to the intersection. You proceed only when it is safe and does not interfere with other road users.

question: If another driver behaves aggressively toward you, what should you do?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating them.,b:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.,c:Cut them off to slow them down.
note: When another driver is aggressive, your goal is to avoid escalating the situation. Stay calm, do not make eye contact or respond with gestures, and safely slow down or change lanes so they can pass. Creating distance reduces the chance of a collision or confrontation.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It prevents distractions from other vehicles.,b:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.,c:It helps keep traffic speed consistent.
note: A space cushion is the open area around your vehicle—especially in front—that gives you time and room to react. If a driver ahead brakes suddenly or a hazard appears, extra space lets you slow, stop, or steer away safely without needing extreme or unsafe maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn.,b:Get off at the next exit and come back safely.,c:Back up on the shoulder to return to the exit.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway or interstate, keep going to the next exit. From there, you can safely re-enter and return to your intended exit. Never stop, back up, or make a U-turn on the highway, as these actions are extremely dangerous and usually illegal.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, the best action is to:
options: a:Get out of the car and walk for help.,b:Stay in your car and wait for help.,c:Lay down in your car and sleep.,d:Walk into the road to attract passing motorists.
note: Staying in your vehicle during a snowstorm is usually safest. Your car provides shelter, is easier for rescuers to see, and protects you from getting lost or exposed to cold. Run the engine only periodically for heat with a slightly open window and a cleared exhaust pipe to avoid carbon monoxide poisoning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not pass:
options: a:On a hill or curve where your view is blocked.,b:When a school bus has flashing red lights and is stopped to load/unload children (unless you are on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical median).,c:When approaching or driving through an intersection.,d:All of the above.
note: You must not pass when you cannot see far enough ahead, such as on hills or curves, because an oncoming vehicle may appear suddenly. You must also not pass when a school bus has flashing red lights and is stopped to load or unload children, unless you are on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical median. Passing near or at intersections is also unsafe because cross traffic or turning vehicles may enter your path.

question: Roads tend to become very slippery:
options: a:When it has been raining for an hour or more.,b:Only after several days of rain.,c:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,d:When the temperature is above 100°F.
note: When rain first begins, oil and debris on the road mix with the water and create a very slick surface. This is why the first 10–15 minutes of a rainstorm are especially dangerous. Slow down, avoid sudden braking or turning, and increase your following distance during this time.

question: What is the safest way to pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Slow down, change lanes if possible, and give the bicyclist plenty of space (at least the minimum distance required by law).,b:Honk at the bicyclist to alert them as you pass.,c:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass the bicyclist more quickly.
note: The safest way to pass a bicyclist is to slow down and give them plenty of space, following your state’s minimum passing distance (often at least 3 feet, and more at higher speeds). Do not honk in a way that could startle them, and never drive in a bicycle lane except where allowed to safely turn or when specifically permitted by law.

question: Which of the following is NOT a factor in determining your vehicle's stopping distance?
options: a:Steering ability.,b:Braking distance.,c:Reaction distance.,d:Perception time.
note: Total stopping distance is the distance your vehicle travels from the moment you see a hazard until you come to a complete stop. It includes perception distance (seeing and recognizing the hazard), reaction distance (moving your foot to the brake), and braking distance (while the brakes are slowing the car). Steering ability does not directly change how far it takes you to stop in a straight line.

question: What are the consequences for parking illegally in a space designated for disabled drivers?
options: a:No negative consequences.,b:Only a small fine.,c:Fines and possible jail time and other penalties.
note: Illegally parking in a space reserved for people with disabilities is a serious violation. States typically impose large fines, and repeat or extreme violations can lead to additional penalties such as court action, loss of certain privileges, or vehicle impoundment. These penalties are meant to keep accessible spaces available for those who genuinely need them.

question: You must stop at an intersection when you see which signal?
options: a:A steady yellow light.,b:A yellow arrow.,c:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, you may proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe. A steady yellow or yellow arrow is a warning that the signal is about to turn red; you should prepare to stop if you can do so safely, but they do not always require an immediate stop the way a flashing red does.

question: A single dashed yellow line separating two directions of traffic means:
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Drivers may not pass.,d:A turn lane is ahead.
note: A single dashed yellow line between opposing lanes of traffic means vehicles traveling in either direction may pass if it is safe and legal. Before passing, you must ensure there is enough clear distance ahead, no oncoming traffic close by, and no signs or markings prohibiting passing.

question: If you are waiting to turn left and opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane is clear.,b:Wait until you can see all the lanes you must cross before making the turn.,c:Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
note: When turning left, you must not begin your turn until you can clearly see all lanes you must cross and are sure you can complete the turn safely. If opposing traffic or large vehicles block your view, wait until your view is clear. Never rely on another driver waving you through, and do not accelerate blindly into a gap you cannot fully see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the light.,b:Be prepared to stop if it is safe to do so.,c:Stop in the center of the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and be prepared to stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to the intersection to stop safely when the light turns yellow, continue through with caution rather than braking abruptly and risking a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time and there are no signs or signals, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The car approaching from the left has the right-of-way.,b:The car approaching from the right has the right-of-way.,c:The car whose driver sounds the horn first has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), drivers must yield to vehicles approaching from their right when they arrive at the same time. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when no other control is present.

question: If you must drive in fog, what should you do with your lights?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights.,b:Turn on your parking lights.,c:Turn on your low beam headlights.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights because their light aims down at the road and reduces glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and can make it harder to see. Use fog lights too if your vehicle has them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left you must yield the right-of-way to which road users?
options: a:Drivers already in the intersection only.,b:Oncoming traffic and any pedestrians in the intersection or crosswalk.,c:Vehicles behind you that started moving last.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, including cars, motorcycles, and bicycles, and to pedestrians who are in or entering the crosswalk. Only turn when there is a safe gap and all road users with the right‑of‑way have cleared your path.

question: If you are involved in a crash and your vehicle is blocking traffic, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.,b:Never move your vehicle under any circumstances.,c:Wait for police before moving anything.
note: After a minor crash, if no one is seriously injured and the vehicles are drivable, you should move them out of the traffic lane to the shoulder or a safe area. This helps prevent additional collisions. You must still stop, exchange information, and provide aid if needed.

question: What is the most common color used for general warning signs?
options: a:Red.,b:Yellow.,c:Green.
note: General warning signs are usually diamond‑shaped and yellow with black symbols or wording. They alert drivers to conditions such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or other potential hazards ahead.

question: What does a single broken yellow center line indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions; passing is allowed when safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions; passing is never allowed.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
note: A single broken yellow center line means traffic in the two lanes moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed in either direction when it is safe. You must still check for oncoming traffic, ensure you have enough space to pass, and obey any additional signs or markings.

question: To help ensure your physical condition does not impair your driving, you should:
options: a:Know how any medication affects your ability to drive.,b:Keep physically fit and have regular medical check-ups.,c:Drive within your physical limitations.,d:All of the above.
note: Safe driving depends on your physical and mental condition. You should know how any medication affects your alertness, keep yourself in good health with regular check-ups, and avoid driving in ways that exceed your physical limitations. Doing all of these helps prevent impairment-related crashes.

question: What does a flashing red light on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:The traffic signal is broken.,b:The same thing as a stop sign.,c:You do not have to come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing red light means you must stop completely, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop at the limit line or before entering the crosswalk or intersection, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: When may you park or stop along the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:If you need to look at a map for directions.,b:Only in an emergency.,c:As long as you turn on your four-way (emergency) flashers.,d:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
note: On freeways, stopping or parking on the shoulder is only allowed for emergencies, such as a breakdown, flat tire, or medical problem. Non-emergency stops, like checking directions, are not allowed. If you must stop for an emergency, pull as far off the road as possible and use your hazard lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may a driver text while driving?
options: a:Never; you should not text while the vehicle is moving.,b:Only when the vehicle is safely parked out of traffic.,c:Only when using a hands-free system for voice calls, not for typing or reading texts.
note: Texting while driving is prohibited except for emergency calls; looking away from the road to text greatly increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you start a left turn on multilane one-way streets or highways?
options: a:The middle of the intersection.,b:The left lane.,c:The right lane.
note: On a multilane one-way street or highway, you must start a left turn from the leftmost lane that is lawfully available for your direction of travel. This keeps you out of the path of faster traffic on the right and makes your turn more predictable and safer for others.

question: Which road areas tend to freeze first in cold or wet weather?
options: a:Roads in the sun.,b:Shaded sections of the road.,c:Flat open areas.
note: Shaded areas of the road, such as those under trees, bridges, or alongside buildings, freeze first and thaw last because they receive less sunlight. Even when the rest of the road looks clear, these spots can still be icy and slippery, so you should slow down and use extra caution when driving through them.

question: What color lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:White.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: White lines are used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, such as on multi-lane city streets and freeways. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Knowing this helps you quickly understand whether you are allowed to pass and what direction traffic should be moving in each lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:Stop at the nearest point where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersection.,b:You are not required to stop.,c:Always stop only after entering the intersection to get a better view.
note: If there is a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can clearly see approaching traffic. This ensures you obey the stop requirement while positioning your vehicle where you can safely judge when it is clear to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.,b:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.,c:Stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
note: When entering a street from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must stop before the sidewalk or edge of the roadway and yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the road. Only proceed when there is a safe gap. You cannot force others to slow or move; the responsibility is on you to wait until the way is clear.

question: When roads are slippery, what adjustment should you make?
options: a:Drive the same as on dry roads.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Use alternate routes only.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less traction and it takes longer to stop. Increasing your following distance gives you more time and space to brake gently and avoid skids or rear‑end collisions.

question: How should you react when you are behind a transit bus signaling to re-enter a traffic lane?
options: a:Quickly pass the bus before it merges.,b:Yield the right-of-way and allow the bus to re-enter.,c:Expect the bus to yield to you.
note: Transit buses are large, slow to maneuver, and make frequent stops. When they signal to re‑enter traffic, you should yield by slowing down or changing lanes if safe so they can merge smoothly and safely back into the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp should do what?
options: a:Force their way into traffic.,b:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.,c:Stop at the ramp until a gap appears.
note: Traffic already on the interstate has the right‑of‑way. Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, then merge when there is a safe gap, yielding to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: In which situations is it especially important to slow down?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads.,b:At intersections or railroad crossings.,c:When the road is wet or slippery.,d:All of the above.
note: You should slow down whenever conditions reduce visibility or traction or increase risk: on narrow or winding roads, at intersections and railroad crossings where cross‑traffic may appear, and on wet or slippery roads where stopping distances are longer.

question: What does an 'End school zone' sign mean?
options: a:The end of a reduced school zone speed limit.,b:The beginning of a reduced school speed zone.,c:An increased possibility of encountering pedestrians ahead.
note: An “End school zone” sign tells you that the special reduced school‑zone speed limit no longer applies. After passing the sign, you may resume the posted regular speed limit if conditions are safe.

question: A sign that reads 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' indicates what?
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign.,b:You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced zone.,c:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at the next speed limit sign.
note: A “Reduced speed, 35 mph” sign means the new 35 mph limit applies starting exactly at that sign. You must already be slowed to 35 mph by the time you reach it, not sometime later.

question: Which of these is an effect alcohol can have on drivers?
options: a:It impairs your thinking ability.,b:It slows your reaction time.,c:It gives you a feeling of false confidence.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol affects driving in several ways at the same time: it impairs your thinking and judgment, slows your reaction time, and often makes you feel more confident than you really should be. Any of these effects can make you an unsafe driver.

question: Which actions help prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Reduce speed when driving in the rain.,b:Ensure tires are properly inflated.,c:Ensure tires have good tread depth.,d:All of the above.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. You reduce this risk by slowing down in wet conditions and by keeping your tires in good condition—properly inflated and with enough tread depth to channel water away.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes moving in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.,b:Lanes moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed anytime.,c:Lanes moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A double solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means no passing is allowed for vehicles traveling either way. You may cross it only to turn left when it is safe and legal to do so, not to pass.

question: How can you help avoid drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Keep the radio on loudly.,b:Slow down your speed.,c:Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
note: To avoid drowsiness on long trips, plan to stop regularly so you can rest, walk, and stretch. Short breaks help you stay alert much more effectively than turning up the radio or changing your speed.

question: When the center of the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If you are on an expressway.,c:If traffic is clear.,d:Never.
note: A solid yellow line with a broken yellow line means only the side with the broken line may pass. If the broken line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass, but only when you can see that oncoming traffic is clear and it is safe to complete the maneuver.

question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:When you have to stop quickly.,b:When passing another car.,c:If you have lost control of your vehicle or need to warn others of immediate danger.
note: Use your horn to warn other road users of a hazard when they might not see you, such as if you are losing control, a driver is about to hit you, or a pedestrian is stepping into your path. Do not use the horn just because you are stopping quickly or to signal routine passing; it is for warning of immediate danger, not for expressing frustration.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers,b:Human error,c:Bad weather,d:Vehicle defects
note: Most crashes are caused by human error, such as following too closely, speeding, distraction, or misjudging gaps, rather than by weather or mechanical failure. Safe driving habits and attention can prevent many of these errors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you use your turn signals?
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.,d:All of the above.
note: You must signal any time you change direction or move your vehicle laterally, including when changing lanes, turning, pulling into or out of a parking space, and entering traffic from a curb, driveway, or alley. Signaling lets other road users anticipate your actions and reduces the risk of collisions.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do about your vehicle lights?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Drive using your four-way flashers.,c:Use only your parking lights.
note: At dusk, dawn, or on overcast days, turn on your headlights so others can see you more easily, even if you can see well. Use low beams when there is oncoming traffic or when following another vehicle so you do not blind other drivers. Do not drive with only parking lights or with four-way flashers in normal conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in line at a stop sign and the cross traffic is clear after cars ahead pass, what must you do?
options: a:May proceed through the intersection without stopping again.,b:Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,c:May slowly roll past the stop sign.
note: At a stop sign, each driver must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or sign before entering the intersection. Even if cars ahead of you have already stopped and gone, you must make your own full stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe.

question: Drivers should be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:
options: a:They always have the right-of-way.,b:They obey different traffic laws than motor vehicles.,c:They can be more difficult to see in traffic.,d:They are always traveling at the same speed as traffic.
note: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and less visible than cars and trucks, so they can be hidden in blind spots or blend into the background. Drivers must scan carefully, check mirrors and blind spots, and give them extra space because they are more vulnerable in a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow center line, what does that tell you?
options: a:The road is under repair.,b:You are on a one-way road.,c:You are on a two-way road where passing is allowed when it is safe.
note: A yellow center line means traffic on the road is moving in opposite directions, so you are on a two‑way road. A broken yellow line allows passing when it is safe and legal: you must check for oncoming traffic, ensure you have enough clear distance, and never cross the line if your view is blocked or passing is otherwise unsafe.

question: What is the effect of eating or drinking while driving?
options: a:It eliminates the need for seat belts.,b:It can cause distraction and lead to driving errors.,c:It makes you a better driver because you are not hungry.
note: Eating or drinking while driving is a form of distracted driving. It can take one or both hands off the wheel and your eyes or attention off the road, making it easier to drift out of your lane, miss hazards, or react too slowly to sudden changes in traffic.

question: What is a \No zone\"?"
options: a:A designated no passing zone.,b:A one-way traffic area.,c:The large blind spots around a truck or other large vehicle.,d:A restricted parking area.
note: A "No‑Zone" is the large blind spot around trucks and other big vehicles where the driver cannot easily see you, especially directly behind, alongside the trailer, and close in front. If you stay in these areas, the truck driver may not know you are there, so you should avoid lingering and pass quickly and safely.

question: What is one effective way to avoid needing to make an emergency stop in traffic?
options: a:Honk your horn frequently.,b:Look ahead and keep a safe following distance.,c:Drive only in the right lane.
note: Maintaining a safe following distance and scanning ahead lets you react to hazards gradually and avoid sudden stops.

question: If you are being tailgated and there is no right lane, what should you do?
options: a:Brake suddenly to get them to back off.,b:Wait until the way ahead is clear and gently reduce your speed to encourage them to pass.,c:Speed up to create more distance.
note: If you cannot move right, wait for a clear stretch and then gently reduce speed so the tailgater can pass; never brake abruptly.

question: Is it ever permissible to drive around or under a lowering or raising railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Only if you can do so without damaging the gate.,b:If an approaching train is not too close.,c:No — you must not go around or under the gate while it is moving.
note: Never drive around or under a crossing gate; wait until signals stop and gates are fully raised before crossing.

question: Before backing out of a driveway with children nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn so the children will hear you.,b:Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.,c:Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
note: When children are nearby, get out of the vehicle and check behind it before backing up rather than relying solely on mirrors or sensors.

question: The effect that lack of sleep has on driving ability is most similar to the effect of which substance?
options: a:The effect that alcohol has.,b:The effect that amphetamines have.,c:The effect that anger has.,d:The effect that high caffeine intake has.
note: Fatigue impairs driving in ways similar to alcohol; for example, 18 hours awake can impair driving similar to a BAC of 0.05%.

question: If an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approaches while you are on a one-way street, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers turned on.,b:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,c:Speed up and take the nearest exit.
note: On any road, including a one-way street, you must yield to approaching emergency vehicles using lights or siren. Safely move your vehicle to the nearest edge or curb of the roadway—right or left on a one-way street—and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road indicate?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road, or when otherwise specifically allowed by law, but not to pass another vehicle.

question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, you should glance:
options: a:Over your right shoulder.,b:At your side mirror.,c:Over your left shoulder.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; areas not visible in your mirrors are called blind spots. When changing lanes to the left, you must quickly glance over your left shoulder to check the left blind spot before moving, while still using your mirrors and signal.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or lights, how should you proceed?
options: a:Turn down your radio to listen for a train.,b:Slow down, look and listen, and proceed only when you are sure no train is coming.,c:Only continue once a flagger clears you to do so.
note: A crossbuck alone means you must treat the railroad crossing like a yield sign. Slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and be prepared to stop. Proceed across the tracks only when you are sure no train is coming and it is safe to cross without stopping on the tracks.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign you should:
options: a:Be ready to drive faster than the train.,b:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,c:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,d:Speed up to cross before the train arrives.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching tracks and must use extra caution. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if a train is nearby or signals are activated. Never try to beat a train or go around lowered gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Continue to the next exit and re-enter the freeway to reach your destination.,b:Make a U-turn through the median.,c:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.,d:Stop on the freeway and reverse to the exit.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, stay calm and continue driving to the next exit. Stopping, backing up, or making a U-turn on the freeway or median is extremely dangerous and illegal in most places. Once you reach the next exit, you can safely leave the freeway, turn around if needed, and re-enter to reach your destination.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line but not from the lane next to the solid line.,b:Passing is permitted from either direction.,c:Passing from the lane next to the solid line is allowed.,d:Traffic moves in the same direction on both sides.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. Passing is allowed only for drivers in the lane next to the broken line, and only when it is safe. Drivers in the lane next to the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass.

question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:
options: a:May be safely held by a strong adult in a crash.,b:Will be safe if standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,c:Will not be hurt in a crash because they are small.,d:Must be properly secured in an appropriate child restraint or safety seat.
note: Small children must always be secured in a properly installed child safety seat or restraint that matches their age, height, and weight. In a crash, an adult cannot safely hold a child, and standing or being loose in the vehicle is extremely dangerous. Proper restraints greatly reduce the risk of serious injury or death.

question: Which factor greatly affects your ability to stop safely?
options: a:The condition of the road surface.,b:The time of day.,c:The color of your vehicle.
note: Stopping distance depends heavily on road surface conditions. Wet, icy, snowy, or gravel roads reduce traction and make it take much longer to stop, so you must slow down and increase your following distance. Time of day or vehicle color do not significantly change how quickly your vehicle can stop.

question: While driving uphill behind a heavy truck, what should you know about the truck's speed?
options: a:You may not be able to legally pass the truck.,b:The truck may be traveling at a speed slower than the posted speed limit.,c:You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
note: Heavy trucks often slow down when going uphill because of their weight and engine limits, so they may travel below the posted speed limit. When following a truck uphill, be prepared for slower speeds and only pass if it is legal, safe, and you have enough clear distance—never attempt risky passes on hills.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns solid yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.,b:Consider it the same as a caution sign and speed up through the intersection.,c:Stop immediately wherever you are.
note: A solid yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are so close that stopping would require hard braking or might cause a rear-end collision, you should continue through carefully.

question: What does checking your blind spot by turning your head before changing lanes represent?
options: a:A bad driving habit.,b:A good driving habit.,c:An unnecessary action.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot cover. Turning your head briefly to check these areas before changing lanes is a key part of safe driving and helps you avoid collisions with vehicles riding alongside you.

question: Your first response to reduced visibility should be to:
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Turn on your windshield wipers.,d:Increase cabin lighting.
note: When visibility is reduced, you must make your vehicle easier for others to see. Turning on your low-beam headlights is typically your first response so you can see and be seen. You should then adjust your speed and use wipers as needed for conditions.
