question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:
options: a:Retain an automatic right-of-way to turn with no yielding.,b:May still turn in the arrow’s direction but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:May no longer turn and must go straight.,d:Must wait for a flashing yellow before turning.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn with the right-of-way. When it changes to a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction, but the turn is no longer protected. You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians and turn only when it is safe.

question: What is a blind spot?
options: a:An area you cannot see without moving your head.,b:A place directly behind your vehicle.,c:An area you can see in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see with your mirrors alone. They are usually along the sides and slightly to the rear. To check them, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you meet an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road, what must you allow?
options: a:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.,b:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Pull completely off the road and stop.,d:Speed up and pass quickly.
note: On a narrow two-way road, each driver must share the roadway so that both vehicles can pass safely. You must allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road and adjust your position and speed so neither vehicle is forced off the roadway.

question: Anything that causes you to do which of the following could lead to a crash?
options: a:Take your eyes off the road.,b:Take your hands off the wheel.,c:Take your attention away from driving.,d:Any of the above.
note: Anything that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving is a distraction and can quickly lead to a crash. Safe drivers keep their full visual, physical, and mental attention on driving at all times.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights because their light aims down at the road and reduces glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and can actually make it harder to see. Use fog lights too if your vehicle has them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, it is usually best to:
options: a:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,b:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic and merge when safe.,c:Turn on your hazard lights until you are fully on the freeway.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.
note: When entering a freeway, use the on-ramp and acceleration lane to build up speed so you match the flow of traffic. Signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge when there is a safe gap. Freeway traffic has the right-of-way, so avoid stopping on the ramp unless absolutely necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A speed limit sign indicates what?
options: a:The suggested speed to travel on a road under ideal conditions.,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.,c:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under dangerous conditions.,d:The minimum safe speed at all times.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum (or sometimes minimum) legal speed allowed under ideal conditions. You must slow down below the posted limit when weather, traffic, or road conditions are poor so that you can drive safely and maintain control.

question: Which driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snow-covered roads?
options: a:Engage four-wheel drive on your vehicle.,b:Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.,c:Add extra weight to your vehicle to improve traction.,d:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.
note: On icy or snow‑covered roads, the safest technique is to slow down and leave much more space between you and the vehicle ahead. Lower speed gives you more time to react, and extra following distance allows for the much longer stopping distances on slippery surfaces. Features like four‑wheel drive can help you get moving, but they do not help you stop more quickly and are never a substitute for cautious driving.

question: When driving on major highways, what practices help avoid 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Keep your eyes fixed on a distant point.,b:Stay alert, keep your eyes moving, and take regular breaks.,c:Drive without breaks until your destination.
note: To avoid highway hypnosis, you should stay mentally alert, keep your eyes moving by scanning the road and mirrors, and take regular breaks to rest. Staring at one fixed point can make you drowsy and less aware of changing traffic conditions. Short stops to stretch, get fresh air, or switch drivers help you stay focused and safe on long trips.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady yellow traffic light, how should you respond?
options: a:Speed up to avoid a red light.,b:Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely; proceed only if you are too close to stop safely or already in the intersection.,c:Continue because you have the right-of-way.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are so close that stopping suddenly would cause a rear‑end collision or you are already in the intersection, continue through carefully. Never speed up to beat the red light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where another vehicle arrives at the same time and is on your right, you should:
options: a:Speed up and get through the intersection.,b:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Drive into the intersection and force the other vehicle to stop.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. Slowing down and letting the driver on your right go first reduces confusion and prevents collisions. Never speed up or try to force another driver to stop in this situation.

question: Which effect does alcohol have on driving-related abilities?
options: a:Puts you to sleep.,b:Wakes you up.,c:Slows reflexes and reaction time.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity, which in turn slows your reflexes and reaction time. This makes it harder to judge distances, stay in your lane, and respond quickly to hazards, greatly increasing your risk of a crash. Even small amounts of alcohol can impair driving ability.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually what color and must be obeyed?
options: a:White,b:Blue,c:Green
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must or must not do (such as speed limits, no parking, or one-way). In the U.S., they are most commonly white with black or red symbols or lettering, and they are legally enforceable, meaning you must obey them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb:
options: a:Is necessary only if other traffic is present.,b:Is required by law and is a good driving habit.,c:Is necessary only during the maneuver itself.,d:Is optional on private roads.
note: You are legally required to signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from the curb, and you must do so in advance—typically for at least the last 100 feet in city driving (and more at higher speeds). Signaling early lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians anticipate your actions and reduces the chance of a collision.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, how should you react?
options: a:Always sound your horn when children are present.,b:Always stop whether a stop sign is posted or not.,c:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. You should slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop. Always yield to pedestrians in or entering a crosswalk, but you are not required to stop if no pedestrians are present and there is no stop sign or signal requiring a stop.

question: To reduce the effects of oncoming headlight glare at night, where should you look?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:Toward the right side of the road ahead.,c:Over your shoulder.
note: At night, bright oncoming headlights can temporarily blind you. To reduce glare, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane line as a guide, rather than staring directly into the oncoming lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on blind curves?
options: a:Follow the posted speed limit and any advisory speed signs for the curve.,b:Drive 20 mph on all blind curves unless otherwise posted.,c:Drive 40 mph on all blind curves unless otherwise posted.,d:Drive 55 mph on all blind curves unless otherwise posted.
note: There is no single default speed limit specifically for blind curves in U.S. traffic law. You must obey the general posted speed limit for the road and any yellow advisory speed plaques posted for a particular curve. If visibility is limited or the curve is sharp, you must slow to a safe speed that allows you to stop within the distance you can see ahead, even if that is below the posted limit.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?
options: a:When turning left or right.,b:Only when backing up.,c:Before changing lanes.,d:Whenever you change your vehicle's position, such as turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.
note: You must check your blind spots any time you change the position of your vehicle in a way that could affect nearby traffic, not just when changing lanes. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb. Mirrors do not show everything; a quick glance over your shoulder helps you see vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians in areas your mirrors miss.

question: What should you remember when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:Wet roads reduce traction and can cause hydroplaning, especially just after it starts to rain.,b:Wet roads are only dangerous during heavy downpours.,c:Wet pavement has about the same traction as dry pavement if you have good tires.
note: On wet pavement, your tires have less traction and can ride up on a thin film of water, a situation called hydroplaning. This greatly reduces your ability to steer or stop. Wet roads are especially slippery just after rain begins, when oil and dirt rise to the surface, and you should slow down and leave extra space for stopping.

question: How should you position your wheels when parking uphill on a street with a curb?
options: a:Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.,b:Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.,c:Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.,d:Keep your front wheels straight ahead.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will gently touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic. On a downhill with a curb, you turn the wheels toward the curb so the front of the tire will block the roll.

question: What do downward-facing triangular road signs indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Yield.,c:Construction zones.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is the standard shape for a yield sign. It tells you to slow down and be ready to stop if necessary to let other road users with the right-of-way go first.

question: For drivers 21 or older, at what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is it illegal to drive?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: In most U.S. states, including Colorado, it is illegal for drivers 21 and older to operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. However, you can be impaired at lower levels, so it is safest not to drive after drinking at all.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a flagger directs traffic in a construction zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the directions given by the flagger.,b:Assume the flagger is mistaken and follow other vehicles.,c:Ignore the flagger and proceed as usual.
note: In work zones, a flagger has the same legal authority as a traffic signal or police officer. You must follow the flagger’s directions, even if they differ from normal signs or what other drivers are doing, to keep workers and drivers safe.

question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement indicate?
options: a:Drivers in the lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow when proceeding, unless otherwise directed by signs or signals.,b:Drivers in the lane may make the movement if they choose.,c:Drivers must always come to a complete stop before making the movement.,d:The arrow only applies when traffic signals are not working.
note: Lane-use arrows painted on the pavement show what movement is allowed or required from that lane, such as straight, left turn, or right turn. When you are in a lane marked with a turn-only arrow, you must make that movement and also obey any traffic signals or signs that control the intersection.

question: When interacting with pedestrians, what must a driver do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way even if the pedestrian is crossing illegally.,b:Make certain the pedestrian is aware of the vehicle.,c:Yield only when the pedestrian has the legal right-of-way.
note: Drivers must use extreme care around pedestrians and do everything possible to avoid hitting them. Even if a pedestrian is crossing illegally, you are still required to yield when necessary to prevent a collision and ensure their safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should always signal when:
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,d:All of the above.
note: Turn signals let other road users know what you plan to do. You should always signal before changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, and when entering traffic from an alley, driveway, or parking area so others have time to react safely.

question: Which factors influence how alcohol affects a person?
options: a:How much time passes between drinks.,b:The amount of food in the stomach.,c:The body weight of the individual.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol’s effect on the body depends on several factors, including how quickly you drink, how much you drink, your body weight, and whether you have food in your stomach. Drinking the same amount of alcohol in a shorter time, drinking on an empty stomach, or having a lower body weight will generally raise your blood alcohol concentration more.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left and oncoming traffic is heavy when the light is green, what is a safe choice?
options: a:Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.,b:Use the next intersection.,c:Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
note: If you cannot safely turn left because of heavy oncoming traffic, a safe option is to go through the intersection and use the next legal opportunity to turn.

question: If you see a driver in the vehicle ahead who appears distracted (e.g., driving with one hand while conversing), you should:
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space.,b:Assume they will correct their behavior.,c:Follow closely to observe them.,d:Try to signal them to drive differently.
note: When you see a driver who appears distracted, increase your following distance and give them extra space. Distracted drivers may brake suddenly, drift in their lane, or miss traffic signals, so you should be prepared for unexpected actions rather than following closely or trying to correct their behavior.

question: A green arrow signal displayed for turns means:
options: a:It is used only on one-way streets.,b:Has the same meaning as a circular green light, but traffic must turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.,c:Means you may proceed in any direction once clear.,d:Means you must wait for a circular green light as well.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow. Oncoming traffic, bicycles, and pedestrians facing a red light must yield to you, so you may proceed carefully in the direction of the arrow only. It does not allow you to go straight or turn in any other direction.

question: Which statement about changing weather and driving is true?
options: a:A sudden change in weather requires you to change your driving.,b:Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in inclement weather.,c:You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
note: Any sudden change in weather—rain, fog, snow, wind, or ice—requires you to adjust how you drive. You should usually slow down, increase following distance, and turn on appropriate lights so you can see and be seen. Being alert to traffic around you and reducing speed in rain or fog are both parts of this overall adjustment.

question: When may you drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:When the train has passed.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:When the lights have stopped flashing.
note: You must never drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates, even if you think the train has passed or the track looks clear. Another train may be coming, or the signals may still be active. Stay stopped until the gates are fully raised and the warning lights and bells have stopped.

question: When driving in fog, you should:
options: a:Use your high beam headlights to penetrate the fog.,b:Drive cautiously at reduced speed and use your low beam headlights.,c:Open all windows and increase ventilation.,d:Drive at your normal speed if visibility seems sufficient.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights and reduce speed. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Drive cautiously, increase following distance, and be prepared to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit sign indicates:
options: a:The maximum legal driving speed under ideal conditions.,b:Only a suggested speed to help traffic flow.,c:The exact speed required to avoid a ticket.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed on that road in ideal conditions, not a target or guaranteed safe speed. You must drive slower when conditions are poor—such as in rain, fog, heavy traffic, or road work—so you can maintain control and stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer stops you, how should you behave while waiting for the officer to approach?
options: a:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.,b:Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.,c:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.,d:Immediately exit the vehicle to speak with the officer.
note: When stopped by police, stay in your vehicle unless directed otherwise, keep your hands visible on the steering wheel, and wait for instructions. Sudden movements or reaching for documents before the officer arrives can cause concern. Only retrieve your license, registration, and insurance when the officer asks you to.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning left onto a one-way street, you should complete the turn into:
options: a:The right lane of the one-way street.,b:The lane closest to your previous lane (usually the leftmost lane),c:Either lane as long as it’s clear.,d:The farthest lane from your approach.
note: When turning left onto a one‑way street, you must turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from, usually the leftmost lane. This keeps traffic organized and prevents conflicts with vehicles that may be entering or traveling in the other lanes. You can change lanes later when it is safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you approach an uncontrolled intersection?
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed.,b:Approach slowly, be prepared to stop, look in all directions, and proceed only when safe.,c:Yield to other vehicles and pedestrians who arrive first or from your right.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, slow down, scan left-right-left, and be prepared to yield, especially to vehicles already in the intersection or approaching from your right. A full stop is not always required if visibility is good and no traffic is present, but you must approach cautiously and be ready to stop if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on some highways is not dangerous.,b:Speeding can kill.,c:Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
note: Speeding greatly increases both the chance of a crash and how severe injuries will be. Even skilled drivers cannot fully compensate for the longer stopping distances and reduced reaction time that come with higher speeds.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians in the roadway?
options: a:Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks and at intersections.,b:Drivers must use extreme care and be prepared to yield even if a pedestrian is careless, but pedestrians do not always have the right-of-way.,c:Drivers only need to yield if the pedestrian is crossing with a WALK signal.
note: Drivers must use extreme care around pedestrians and should be prepared to yield even when a pedestrian is acting carelessly. However, the law gives pedestrians the right-of-way primarily in marked or unmarked crosswalks and at intersections; a driver is not legally required to yield to a pedestrian who suddenly darts into traffic mid‑block, though the driver must still do everything possible to avoid a collision.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, what is the first positioning step?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Turn your wheels to the right.,c:Pull up even with the car in front of the desired space.
note: For standard parallel parking, after signaling and checking traffic, you first pull up so your vehicle is parallel and even with the car in front of the space. From there you begin backing into the space while turning the wheel as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop where two drivers arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left.,b:The driver on the right.,c:Either driver may proceed without stopping.
note: At a four‑way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps decide who goes first when arrival is simultaneous.

question: A 'No stopping' sign allows stopping only under which condition?
options: a:Long enough to unload packages.,b:To avoid conflict with other traffic.,c:To discharge passengers.,d:To briefly park while running an errand.
note: A No Stopping zone means you may not stop your vehicle there for passengers or loading. You may only stop as necessary to obey traffic signals or signs, follow a police officer’s directions, or avoid a conflict or collision with other traffic.

question: What is the only effective way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee or take a cold shower.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to remove the alcohol.,d:Take an over-the-counter stimulant.
note: Only time lowers your BAC. Your body must metabolize the alcohol, and this process cannot be sped up by coffee, cold showers, exercise, or stimulants. Those may make you feel more awake but do not make you less impaired or reduce your BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who may use a High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane?
options: a:You if you meet the posted HOV occupancy or vehicle-type requirements.,b:You if you are driving more slowly than traffic.,c:Vehicles that have at least the minimum number of occupants shown on the signs or allowed vehicle types (such as buses or motorcycles where permitted).
note: HOV (carpool) lanes are reserved for vehicles that meet the posted occupancy or vehicle-type requirement, such as two or more people per vehicle or certain buses and motorcycles where allowed. You may not use the lane just because you are driving faster or slower than other traffic; you must follow the posted HOV rules.

question: How should you react to a flashing red light at an intersection?
options: a:Stop only if other cars are also approaching the intersection.,b:Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.,c:Stop only if other cars are already within the intersection.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic and pedestrians with the right-of-way, and then proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
options: a:Vehicles already in the roundabout.,b:Bicyclists and pedestrians in the roundabout.,c:Pedestrians and bicyclists as well as vehicles in the roundabout.,d:All of the above.
note: When approaching a roundabout, slow down and yield to all traffic already in the circle, as well as to pedestrians and bicyclists in crosswalks or within the roundabout. Enter only when there is a safe gap.

question: A steady yellow traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:Go through the intersection quickly.,b:Yield to other cars only.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop as the light will soon turn red.,d:The light will immediately turn green.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop before the intersection, unless you are so close that stopping safely is not possible.

question: What driving habit helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.,b:Accelerating quickly.,c:Slowing down gradually and anticipating traffic flow.
note: Gradual acceleration, gentle braking, and anticipating traffic so you can maintain a steady speed all reduce fuel use. Rapid starts and frequent hard stops waste gasoline.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection is equivalent to what sign?
options: a:A yield sign.,b:A slow sign.,c:A stop sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must stop completely, just as you would at a stop sign, then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: If another driver cuts you off, what is the best response?
options: a:Flash your high beams at the other driver.,b:Pull next to them and yell.,c:Let it go and continue driving safely.
note: If another driver cuts you off, staying calm and continuing to drive safely helps prevent road rage and further danger. Do not confront or retaliate against the other driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it illegal and unsafe to attempt to pass another vehicle?
options: a:On hills and curves.,b:At controlled intersections only.,c:In urban parking lots only.
note: Passing is especially dangerous where you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic, such as on hills and curves. Many states also prohibit passing at intersections and railroad crossings for the same safety reasons.

question: Which is a safe practice on potentially slippery roads?
options: a:Always drive at the maximum posted speed.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,c:Slow down.
note: On slippery roads, you should reduce speed, make gentle steering and braking inputs, and increase following distance. Avoid cruise control so you can respond quickly to changes in traction.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, you should look:
options: a:Directly at the headlights to signal them.,b:Toward the left side of the road.,c:Toward the right side of the road.,d:Into the centerline of the road.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, you should briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide. This reduces glare, helps prevent temporary blindness, and still lets you keep track of your lane position.

question: To drive safely at night, you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Not drive if you are tired.,c:Make sure your headlights are working properly.,d:All of the above.
note: Safe night driving means seeing and being seen and staying alert. You should ensure your headlights work properly, increase your following distance because visibility is reduced, and never drive when you are tired, since fatigue greatly slows your reaction time.

question: How can you reduce the chance of causing a rear-end crash?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops.,b:Before stopping, check mirrors and blind spots.,c:Release the gas to let the vehicle slow before applying the brakes.,d:All of the above.
note: Rear-end crashes often happen when the front driver stops suddenly or without warning. You can reduce this risk by avoiding sudden stops, checking mirrors and blind spots before slowing or stopping, and easing off the gas to begin slowing before you apply the brakes smoothly.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:
options: a:Only the person driving the car.,b:Only passengers on long trips.,c:Only occupants on expressways.,d:All occupants of the vehicle.
note: Seat belts are most effective when every person in the vehicle wears one, regardless of seat position, trip length, or road type. In a crash, belts help keep occupants inside the vehicle and reduce the risk of serious injury or death.

question: Railroad crossings should always be treated as:
options: a:Safe places to stop and wait.,b:Dangerous locations that require caution.,c:Safe locations to park a vehicle temporarily.
note: Railroad crossings are always potential danger zones because trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right of way. Approach every crossing with caution, slow down, look and listen for trains, and obey all warning signs, lights, and gates.

question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do first?
options: a:Back up slowly.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,c:Accelerate as quickly as possible.
note: A green light means you may go if the intersection is clear, but you must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles still in the intersection. Never assume the way is clear just because the light turned green; check for people and traffic before moving.

question: How should you approach railroad tracks when driving?
options: a:Speed up to cross the tracks before the gate is lowered.,b:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,c:Try to drive around a lowered gate.
note: When approaching railroad tracks, you should slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains. Be prepared to stop if warning lights, gates, or signs indicate a train is coming. Never speed up to beat a train or drive around lowered gates, as trains cannot stop quickly and collisions are often fatal.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian walk on?
options: a:Same side of the road on which traffic is moving.,b:Side with the lightest traffic.,c:The side of the road facing oncoming traffic.
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on the side facing oncoming traffic. This allows them to see approaching vehicles and react if needed, and it also makes them more visible to drivers.

question: How should you behave when approaching a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Take the right-of-way and proceed.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Proceed normally without changing speed.
note: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must yield the right-of-way. Slow down well in advance, be prepared to stop, and do not honk or rev your engine. Give them plenty of time and space to cross safely.

question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with its lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.,b:Slow down and, if possible, change lanes away from the stopped vehicle.,c:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
note: If possible, change lanes to leave extra space for stopped emergency or roadside assistance vehicles; otherwise slow down and pass carefully.

question: If you plan to drink socially, what is a safe way to ensure you get home safely?
options: a:Drink coffee before driving.,b:Take a cold shower.,c:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
note: If you plan to drink, the safe choice is to arrange a sober way home, such as riding with a friend who has not been drinking, using a taxi, or a rideshare. Coffee, cold showers, or other tricks do not reduce your blood alcohol concentration or make you safe to drive.

question: When driving in traffic, what is generally the safest approach to speed?
options: a:Drive faster than the flow of traffic.,b:Drive slower than the flow of traffic.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted limits.
note: You should generally travel with the flow of traffic while staying at or below the posted speed limit and adjusting for road, weather, and visibility conditions. Driving much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic increases the risk of collisions.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what should you do first?
options: a:Leave the scene if no one looks injured.,b:Stop your vehicle.,c:Only call the police if your vehicle is completely undamaged.
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop at or near the scene, check for injuries, and provide help and information as required by law. Leaving the scene is illegal. Call 911 if anyone is injured or if there is significant damage, and follow state reporting requirements.

question: How should drivers respond to a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.,b:Honk before passing the bus on its left.,c:Continue when you think most kids are done exiting.,d:Pass slowly without stopping.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers in most situations must come to a complete stop and may not pass the bus. Remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, then proceed with caution, watching for children.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain your normal driving speed.,b:Stop and look for nearby police cars.,c:Yield to pedestrians.
note: When turning right on a green light, you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any traffic already in or close to the intersection. Make the turn at a safe, reduced speed and only when the way is clear.

question: Where is it illegal to park?
options: a:On a hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a marked crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: It is illegal to park on a marked crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane because you block pedestrians and cyclists and create a safety hazard. Parking on a hill or in a parking lot is allowed when you follow posted signs and properly position your vehicle.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:A loss of hearing.,b:Pollution.,c:Carbon monoxide poisoning.
note: A leaky exhaust system can let carbon monoxide, a colorless and odorless poisonous gas, enter the passenger area. Breathing carbon monoxide can quickly cause illness, unconsciousness, or death, so exhaust leaks must be repaired immediately.

question: How should you secure loose objects in your vehicle?
options: a:Place them on the back seat.,b:Put them on the floor near the driver's seat.,c:Secure them so they cannot become hazards in a crash.
note: Loose objects should be secured so they cannot move around. In a sudden stop or crash, unsecured items can become dangerous projectiles or slide into the pedals or steering area, making it harder to control the vehicle.

question: What do round warning signs most often indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Upcoming railroad crossings.,c:No passing zones.
note: In the U.S., round warning signs are used specifically for railroad crossings. When you see a round yellow railroad warning sign, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: What can happen when alcohol is consumed with other drugs?
options: a:The combination can decrease the effects of both substances.,b:The combination can increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.,c:The combination helps cure illnesses faster.
note: Alcohol combined with other drugs often has a multiplying effect, making you more impaired than either substance alone. This can severely affect judgment, coordination, and reaction time, and can also cause dangerous medical reactions.

question: If you drive much slower than the flow of traffic on a two-lane road and cars are backing up, what should you do?
options: a:Continue at your slow speed regardless of following traffic.,b:Pull off the road when safe to let others pass.,c:Refuse to let following cars pass.
note: On a two-lane road, if you are driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic and vehicles are backing up behind you, you should safely pull off the road at the first safe opportunity and let them pass. This reduces driver frustration and the risk of unsafe passing maneuvers, and is required by law in many states when several vehicles are lined up behind a slow-moving vehicle.

question: Which traffic signal indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A flashing red light.,c:A solid yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution, watching carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards. Unlike a flashing red light, you are not required to stop first, but you must be prepared to yield if necessary.

question: Where are stop lines painted on the pavement?
options: a:Next to churches and schools.,b:In curves and on hills.,c:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across the lane at intersections and before pedestrian crosswalks. You must stop with your front bumper behind this line when required to stop by a sign or signal, so that you do not block the crosswalk or intersection.

question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Driving too fast for wet conditions.,b:Excessive stops.,c:Sudden turns.
note: Hydroplaning usually happens when you drive too fast on a wet road. At higher speeds, your tires cannot channel water away quickly enough and begin to ride on top of the water instead of the pavement, causing a loss of steering and braking control. Slowing down in rain and keeping good tire tread greatly reduces this risk.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Stop where you are.,b:Pull over to the right and stop.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle approaching from behind, you must safely move to the right side of the road and stop until it has passed. This creates a clear path for the emergency vehicle and is required in all states, unless directed otherwise by a police officer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:If the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available lane on the right.,b:Even if it means driving off the pavement.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: You may pass on the right only when the vehicle ahead is making or about to make a left turn and there is a legal, paved lane or sufficient space on the roadway to do so safely. You must stay on the roadway and may not drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect your ability to drive?
options: a:Does not affect driving abilities.,b:Helps maintain driver alertness.,c:Is a distracting activity.,d:Is required to stay awake.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction because it can take one or both hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Any activity that diverts your attention, hands, or eyes from driving increases the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit on open mountain highways in Colorado?
options: a:55 mph,b:40 mph,c:20 mph,d:65 mph
note: Colorado law sets the maximum speed limit on open mountain highways at 40 mph unless a different speed is posted. Always follow posted signs, as specific roads may have higher or lower limits based on conditions and design.

question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens to your driving ability?
options: a:Makes you feel less confident.,b:Slows down your reactions.,c:Begins to metabolize itself more quickly.
note: As alcohol builds up in your bloodstream, it slows your reaction time, harms your judgment, and reduces coordination. This makes it harder to notice hazards and respond quickly, greatly increasing your chances of a crash.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying dangerous situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Getting ahead of poor drivers by driving aggressively.,c:Following the vehicle ahead at a close distance.
note: Defensive driving means staying alert, looking ahead, and anticipating what other drivers might do so you can react in time to avoid collisions. You adjust your speed, position, and actions to keep a safe space around your vehicle and reduce risk.

question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a roadway indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in the same direction and drivers may change lanes or pass when safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not permitted.
note: A single broken (dashed) white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following has priority over the others when directing traffic?
options: a:A steady red light,b:A stop sign,c:A police officer directing traffic.
note: A police or traffic officer’s directions always override traffic lights, signs, and pavement markings. When an officer is directing traffic, follow their hand signals even if they conflict with the signal or sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on narrow, winding mountain highways?
options: a:40 mph,b:20 mph,c:55 mph,d:70 mph
note: In Colorado, the statutory speed limit on narrow, winding mountain highways is 20 mph unless a different speed is posted. These roads have sharp curves and limited visibility, so the law sets a lower default limit for safety.

question: Which of the following about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.,b:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or sign.,c:Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.,d:All of the above.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around lowered gates at a railroad crossing. You must stop when a flagger, signal, or sign tells you to, and you should remember that many crossings do not have flashing lights or gates, so you must look and listen carefully.

question: Driving while distracted by any activity typically:
options: a:Is never dangerous.,b:Causes drivers to react more slowly to hazards.,c:Causes drivers to drive faster.,d:Improves driver concentration.
note: Distractions such as phones, eating, or adjusting controls take your eyes, mind, or hands away from driving. This slows your reaction time and makes it harder to notice and respond to hazards in time to avoid a crash.

question: If a driver accumulates the minimum of how many points in a 24-month period will their license be suspended?
options: a:12 points,b:18 points,c:20 points,d:24 points
note: In Colorado, the driver’s license point system allows the DMV to suspend your license if you accumulate too many points in a set time. For adult drivers, getting 18 or more points within a 24‑month period can lead to a suspension. This is why knowing and avoiding point‑generating violations is important.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct response?
options: a:Overcorrect the steering.,b:Turn the steering wheel into the direction of the skid.,c:Turn your steering wheel into traffic.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, you should stay calm, ease off the accelerator and brakes, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, which is generally described as steering in the direction of the skid. This helps the tires regain traction and allows you to recover control smoothly instead of overcorrecting.

question: If you are upset from an incident at work, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Turn the radio up loud to distract yourself.,b:Drive fast to release tension.,c:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving home.
note: Strong emotions like anger or frustration can distract you, slow your reactions, and lead to aggressive driving. If you are upset from something like an incident at work, you should wait a few minutes to calm down before driving so your judgment and focus are not impaired.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety step should you take?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers have buckled theirs.,b:Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,c:Be sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.,d:Only the driver needs to buckle a seat belt.
note: Develop a routine: before starting the engine, buckle your safety belt and ensure that all passengers are also properly restrained.

question: What do two solid yellow centerlines on the pavement mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,b:Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.,c:Passing is not allowed.
note: Two solid yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean passing is prohibited for vehicles traveling in either direction. You may cross these lines only when making a left turn into or out of a driveway or side road, when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal indicates which light will appear next?
options: a:Flashing yellow,b:Steady green,c:Steady red,d:Flashing red
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. It warns you to prepare to stop if you can do so safely, because a steady red light will appear next.

question: Allow a larger space cushion than usual when stopped:
options: a:On an incline (uphill).,b:At an intersection.,c:At a stop sign.,d:When there is no traffic behind you.
note: When you are stopped facing uphill, leave extra space in front of your vehicle. The vehicle ahead may roll backward when starting, and the extra cushion helps prevent a collision.

question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
options: a:Whoever started moving last.,b:The driver.,c:Whoever is slower at the moment.,d:The pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are crossing the roadway, even if there is no traffic signal.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Checking antifreeze and windshield washer fluid is especially important during the winter.,b:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,d:Using snow tires can increase traction on slippery roads.
note: In winter, driving is more difficult because of snow, ice, and reduced visibility. You should check antifreeze and washer fluid, consider using snow tires for better traction, and avoid cruise control on slippery or low-visibility roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you pull over and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?
options: a:On an undivided roadway, regardless of whether it approaches from ahead or behind.,b:Only if it is directly following you in your lane.,c:Only if it is approaching you from the opposite direction on a two-lane road.,d:Only when you are in the right lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using flashing lights and/or a siren, you must pull to the right edge of the road and stop, whether it is coming from behind you or from ahead on an undivided roadway, unless directed otherwise by law or an officer.

question: Guide signs (directional and mileage signs) are typically what color?
options: a:Green,b:Red,c:Yellow
note: Guide signs that give route directions, destinations, and mileage are standardly green with white lettering. This color scheme helps drivers quickly recognize information about where they are and where they are going.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:After changing lanes.,b:Just before changing lanes.,c:At any time.
note: You must signal before you begin changing lanes so other drivers have time to see your signal and adjust. Turn on your signal well in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, then change lanes when it is safe.

question: If a pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.,b:Flash your lights to warn them.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: When a pedestrian is in or about to enter your path, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and should never try to speed up or go around them.

question: When preparing to change lanes, which of these is most important to check?
options: a:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.,b:Check your blind spot.,c:Make sure the lane is clear before entering.,d:Flash your headlights to warn others.
note: Before changing lanes, you must make sure the lane you want to enter is clear. Use a three-step check: signal, check your mirrors, and quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move over when you are certain there is enough space and no vehicle is in or rapidly approaching the lane.

question: Which of the following is NOT an effect of drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time speed up.,b:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,c:You are less alert.
note: Alcohol slows reflexes and reaction time, reduces alertness, and distorts your judgment of speed, distance, and risk. It never speeds up your reactions or improves driving ability.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Hold down the brake pedal.,b:Firmly pump your brakes.,c:Lightly tap the brakes.,d:Shift into neutral.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, you should use the "pump braking" method in an emergency stop: apply firm pressure to the brake pedal, release slightly before the wheels lock, then reapply. This helps you slow quickly while still being able to steer and reduces the chance of skidding.

question: At night, which is the hardest to see?
options: a:Road signs.,b:Pedestrians.,c:Other motorists.,d:Lane markings.
note: At night, pedestrians are much harder to see than reflective road signs, lane markings, or the headlights and taillights of other vehicles. Pedestrians often wear dark clothing and are not illuminated, so drivers must scan carefully and reduce speed in areas where people may be walking.

question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a slash through a symbol means:
options: a:That drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:The indicated action is forbidden.,c:That some drivers must yield to others.,d:That the lane is for high-occupancy vehicles only.
note: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a diagonal slash over a symbol means the action shown is prohibited. For example, a right-turn arrow with a red circle and slash means no right turn at that location.

question: If you discover a vehicle defect that could affect safe operation, you should:
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,b:Drive the vehicle at slower speeds until you can afford to fix it.,c:Ignore it until the next service appointment.
note: Any defect that could affect the safe operation of your vehicle—such as problems with brakes, steering, tires, or lights—should be repaired as soon as possible. Driving with known safety defects increases the risk of a crash and may be illegal.

question: If it starts to sleet or snow while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Keep your windshield and mirrors clear, increase your following distance, and approach other vehicles with caution.,b:Increase your speed to reach your destination sooner.,c:Follow closely to the vehicle ahead to use its traction.,d:Turn off your headlights to reduce glare.
note: When it begins to sleet or snow, reduce speed, increase your following distance, and keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Slippery roads greatly increase stopping distance, so you need more space and time to react to other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a public road from a driveway or private road, you should:
options: a:Force your way into traffic.,b:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,c:Assume you have the right-of-way.
note: When you enter a public road from a driveway or private road, you must always yield to traffic already on the public road. Wait until there is a safe gap and then merge smoothly without forcing your way in.

question: How should you behave when approaching service or maintenance vehicles working on the roadway?
options: a:Treat them the same as any other vehicle.,b:Assume they will yield to you.,c:Yield and use extra caution around them.
note: When approaching service or maintenance vehicles, slow down, be prepared to stop, and give them extra space. Workers may be on or near the roadway, so you must yield the right-of-way when needed and pass with great caution.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving it?
options: a:Assume it operates the same as your car.,b:Hide defects to avoid embarrassing the owner.,c:Familiarize yourself with the vehicle's controls and check for defects.
note: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, adjust the seat and mirrors, locate and test the lights, wipers, horn, gear selector, and brakes, and check for obvious defects. Knowing how everything works helps you react safely in an emergency.

question: Why is night driving typically more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:It is more likely to be raining at night.,b:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,c:Cars overheat more quickly at night.
note: Night driving is harder because you can see less of the road and surroundings. Headlights limit how far and wide you can see, and glare from other vehicles can further reduce visibility, so you should slow down and use proper lighting.

question: If a transit bus is signaling to re-enter traffic after stopping, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to alert the bus driver.,b:Move to the left lane or slow to allow the bus to re-enter.,c:Expect the bus to yield to you.
note: When a transit bus signals to re-enter traffic, you should help it merge safely by changing lanes if possible or slowing down to create space. Yielding in this way reduces conflicts and protects passengers and other road users.

question: Pentagonal (five-sided) road signs indicate:
options: a:Speed limits.,b:School zones and school crossings.,c:No passing zones.,d:Railroad crossings.
note: Pentagon-shaped (five-sided) signs are used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this shape, be prepared to slow down, watch for children, and obey any reduced speed limits or crossing guards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road you must:
options: a:Use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic to complete the pass when it is safe and legal to do so.,b:Stay entirely in your lane while overtaking.,c:Flash your headlights to demand the vehicle move over.,d:Use the shoulder to pass.
note: On a standard two-lane, two-way road, you must move into the lane used by oncoming traffic to pass a slower vehicle. Only do this where passing is allowed (broken center line), when you have enough clear distance ahead, and when you can return to your lane safely without speeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive slower than the posted speed limit?
options: a:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.,b:Only when driving in rural areas.,c:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
note: You can be cited for driving too slowly if you block or interfere with the normal, safe flow of traffic. Even if you are below the speed limit, you must not impede other drivers unnecessarily; if you need to drive much slower, move to the right and let faster traffic pass when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down before entering the exit ramp.,b:Slow down once moving onto the exit ramp.,c:Keep your speed constant once in the exit ramp.
note: Stay at freeway speed until you are actually in the exit lane or on the exit ramp, then slow down to the posted ramp speed. Braking on the main freeway lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a good general rule to remember about passing other vehicles?
options: a:Pass on the right whenever possible.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.,c:Try to get to the front of any slow-moving traffic so you can see better.
note: A safe approach is to travel with the general flow of traffic (without exceeding the speed limit) and pass only when it is necessary, legal, and safe. Fewer lane changes and passes reduce your chances of a collision.

question: How can a bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws be dealt with?
options: a:They have different rules and cannot be ticketed.,b:They can be ticketed.,c:They will always receive a warning instead of a ticket.
note: Bicyclists are generally required to follow the same traffic laws as motor vehicle drivers. They can be stopped and cited for violations such as running stop signs or red lights, riding against traffic, or failing to use required lights at night.

question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light when approaching it?
options: a:Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.,b:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,c:Treat it like a stop sign and stop.
note: A flashing red traffic signal means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: When making a turn, what should you do to your speed?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Maintain or reduce your speed as needed to maintain control.,c:Vary speed unpredictably.
note: Before and during a turn, you should slow down enough to stay in full control of the vehicle and keep your lane position. Enter the turn at a safe, steady speed; do not accelerate into the turn or vary your speed unpredictably.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on and is blinding you, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights to warn the other driver.,b:Look to the right side of the road until the vehicle passes.,c:Speed up to pass quickly.
note: When an oncoming vehicle’s high beams are blinding you, avoid looking directly at the lights. Instead, glance down and to the right edge of your lane, using the right side of the road as a guide until the vehicle passes.

question: What should you do if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Open the window to get some fresh air.,b:Stop driving and rest.,c:Drink coffee and keep driving.
note: If you feel drowsy while driving, the only safe choice is to stop driving and rest. Short-term tricks like opening a window or drinking coffee do not reliably prevent fatigue-related crashes.

question: A leaking exhaust system can:
options: a:Cause excessive oil use.,b:Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner than usual.,c:Allow exhaust fumes into the passenger compartment and make you drowsy or cause death.,d:Increase brake wear.
note: A leaking exhaust can let carbon monoxide and other poisonous gases enter the passenger area. Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless, and breathing it can make you drowsy, impair your judgment, or even cause death. Any suspected exhaust leak should be repaired immediately.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do with the ignition key?
options: a:Turn off the engine and leave the key in the ignition.,b:Lock the ignition and remove the key.,c:Set the parking brake only.,d:Leave the engine running to maintain cabin heat.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended you must stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

question: What is the shape of a stop sign?
options: a:Rectangle.,b:Octagon.,c:Circle.
note: A stop sign is an octagon, which means it has eight sides. This unique shape helps drivers recognize it quickly, even if visibility is poor or the sign is partially blocked, so they know they must come to a complete stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to an emergency vehicle?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.,c:Only when other vehicles yield.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using a siren and/or flashing red or blue lights. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police officer.

question: Distracted drivers are at a greater risk of a crash when using which device?
options: a:A CD player.,b:A radio.,c:A cell phone (including hands-free).,d:A GPS with voice prompts.
note: Using a cell phone, even hands-free, takes your attention away from driving. Your mind is focused on the conversation instead of the road, which slows reaction time and increases the chance of a crash. Avoid using a phone while driving whenever possible.

question: Which behavior describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Drives slowly at all times.,b:Looks out for the actions of other drivers.,c:Travels at a constant speed.,d:Avoids using mirrors while driving.
note: A good defensive driver constantly scans the road and watches other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists. By anticipating what others might do, you have more time to react to sudden stops, lane changes, or mistakes, which greatly reduces your chances of a collision.

question: How can you avoid collisions caused by other vehicles' blind spots?
options: a:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,b:Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.,c:Glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot cover. Before changing lanes or turning, you must quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to be sure no one is in that blind spot. Relying only on mirrors can cause you to miss a vehicle riding alongside you.

question: When approaching a curve, drivers should:
options: a:Immediately accelerate.,b:Continue slowing until they are driving straight again.,c:Slow down before reaching the curve and accelerate after passing the curve’s midpoint.,d:Brake hard while in the curve.
note: You should slow down before entering a curve so your tires keep good traction and you stay in control. Once you are past the midpoint of the curve and can see the road ahead, you can gently accelerate to return to normal speed. Braking hard in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control.

question: On average, the human body removes about how many standard alcoholic drinks per hour?
options: a:Three drinks per hour.,b:One drink per hour.,c:Two drinks per hour.,d:No measurable amount per hour.
note: Most people’s bodies can process about one standard drink per hour, but this rate varies with body size, sex, food intake, and health. Because alcohol can still impair you even at low levels, you should never rely on metabolism speed to decide if it is safe to drive.

question: Which is the best way to avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Call a taxi after you begin drinking.,b:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,c:Simply tell others 'No thanks, I'm driving' when offered a drink.
note: Planning ahead is the safest way to avoid alcohol‑related crashes. Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive, and arrange a sober driver, taxi, or rideshare. Once you have been drinking, your judgment is already affected, making it harder to make safe choices about driving.

question: What does a steady green arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,c:Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.,d:Must wait for a circular green light as well.
note: A steady green arrow means you are allowed to turn in the direction of the arrow. You must be in the correct lane and still yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection before completing your turn.

question: What do orange-colored road signs typically indicate?
options: a:Work zone signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:School zone signs.,d:Guide signs.
note: Orange road signs are used for temporary traffic control in work and construction zones. They warn that workers, equipment, or changing road conditions may be present and that you should slow down and use extra caution.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Use your high beams.,b:Use your low beams.,c:Use your parking lights.
note: In fog, use low-beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and improve your ability to see lane lines and the edge of the roadway.

question: Which practice helps reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allow extra travel time.,b:Ignore posted speed limits.,c:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.
note: Allowing extra travel time helps you stay calm and avoid feeling rushed, which reduces the temptation to speed, tailgate, or make aggressive maneuvers. Planning ahead and driving patiently are key parts of preventing road rage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway with double solid yellow lines, when may you cross them?
options: a:Cross these lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross these lines to pass other vehicles if clear.,c:Never cross these lines, even to turn.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and generally prohibit passing. However, you may cross them to make a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or private road when it is safe. You must never use a double solid yellow to pass another vehicle.

question: A diamond-shaped road sign typically indicates:
options: a:A road hazard or warning.,b:An interstate route.,c:A school crossing sign only.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are standard warning signs. They alert drivers to potential hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, merging traffic, or pedestrian crossings. They are not used for route markers or limited only to school crossings.

question: Which method will sober someone up after drinking?
options: a:Drinking tomato juice and lime.,b:Drinking hot coffee.,c:Allowing time to pass (only time makes you sober).
note: Only the passage of time will reduce blood alcohol concentration; remedies like coffee, fresh air, or juice do not reduce BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red traffic signal light requires you to do what?
options: a:Stop at the stop line or, if none, before entering any crosswalk or intersection.,b:Slow down and proceed through the intersection.,c:Stop only if there are pedestrians present.
note: On a steady red light you must come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before entering the crosswalk, and if there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. You may only proceed when the light turns green and it is safe, or when a legal turn on red is allowed and clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in an intersection to make a left turn you should:
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left toward the direction of your turn.,b:Signal and keep your wheels straight while waiting.,c:Flash your headlights to warn other drivers.,d:Keep the wheels lightly on the brakes and turned right.
note: When waiting in an intersection to turn left, signal your turn and keep the wheels pointed straight. If another vehicle hits you from behind, straight wheels help prevent your car from being pushed into oncoming traffic. Turn the wheels left only as you begin the actual turn.

question: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren is approaching, what must you do immediately?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop.,b:Pull to the right and slow down.,c:Pull to the right and turn on your vehicle's four-way flashers.
note: When an emergency vehicle using lights and siren approaches, you must move as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stop until it has passed. This creates a clear path for the emergency vehicle and reduces the risk of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Colorado's GDL program, who are you permitted to carry as a passenger during your first six months of holding a driver's license if you are under age 18?
options: a:Any friends under age 21,b:No passengers under age 21 (unless immediate family or accompanied by a parent/guardian),c:Only one passenger under age 21,d:Only siblings
note: In Colorado, minor drivers under age 18 holding a driver's license are restricted from carrying any passengers under age 21 during the first six months, except for immediate family members or if supervised by a parent/guardian.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Colorado's GDL program, how many passengers under the age of 21 can you carry during your second six months of holding a driver's license?
options: a:None,b:One passenger,c:Two passengers,d:No restrictions apply
note: In Colorado, minor drivers under age 18 holding a driver's license may carry up to one passenger under age 21 during their second six months of driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are the minimum auto liability insurance coverage limits required for all motor vehicles registered in Colorado?
note: Colorado requires all drivers to maintain auto liability insurance coverage of at least 25/50/15: $25,000 for bodily injury per person, $50,000 for bodily injury per accident, and $15,000 for property damage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Colorado's Move Over law, if you are unable to change lanes when approaching a stationary emergency or maintenance vehicle with flashing lights on a road with a speed limit of 45 mph or less, you must slow to:
options: a:15 mph,b:20 mph,c:25 mph,d:30 mph
note: Colorado's Move Over law requires drivers approaching stationary emergency/utility vehicles to slow down to a speed of 25 mph if the posted limit is 45 mph or less, or 20 mph below the posted limit if the limit is above 45 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the statutory speed limit on narrow, winding mountain highways in Colorado unless otherwise posted?
options: a:15 mph,b:20 mph,c:25 mph,d:30 mph
note: In Colorado, the statutory speed limit on narrow, winding mountain highways is 20 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the statutory speed limit on open mountain highways in Colorado unless otherwise posted?
options: a:25 mph,b:30 mph,c:35 mph,d:40 mph
note: In Colorado, the statutory speed limit on open mountain highways is 40 mph unless otherwise posted.
